+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Refresh the RuleSpec-owned adjudication shapes vendored into this binding.
+
+The binding validator deliberately imports no RefSpec or RuleSpec package
+code. This development-time generator is the only package-aware side of that
+boundary: it reads compiler output through the installed
+``rulespec_conformance.contract.resources`` accessor, writes plain Turtle
+beside the Atlas shapes, and records exact source and output digests.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from rulespec_conformance.contract import VERSION, resources
+
+BINDING_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+OUTPUT_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"
+LOCK_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.lock.json"
+RESOURCE_NAMES = ("machine-adjudication", "resolver-proof-record")
+
+
+def _digest(payload: bytes) -> str:
+    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _canonical_json(value: object) -> bytes:
+    return (
+        json.dumps(
+            value,
+            ensure_ascii=False,
+            allow_nan=False,
+            sort_keys=True,
+            separators=(",", ":"),
+        ).encode("utf-8")
+        + b"\n"
+    )
+
+
+def render() -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
+    parts = [
+        "# GENERATED by tools/refresh_rulespec_adjudication_shapes.py.",
+        "# Source: rulespec-conformance compiler output; do not edit here.",
+        f"# Rulespec contract version: {VERSION}",
+        "",
+    ]
+    source_rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
+    for name in RESOURCE_NAMES:
+        text = resources.shacl_sparql(name, family="analysis")
+        payload = text.encode("utf-8")
+        source_rows.append(
+            {
+                "accessor": (
+                    "rulespec_conformance.contract.resources."
+                    f"shacl_sparql({name!r}, family='analysis')"
+                ),
+                "byteLength": len(payload),
+                "digest": _digest(payload),
+                "name": name,
+            }
+        )
+        parts.extend((text.rstrip(), ""))
+    output = "\n".join(parts).encode("utf-8")
+    lock = _canonical_json(
+        {
+            "format": "RulespecAdjudicationShapeLock",
+            "formatVersion": "1.0",
+            "output": {
+                "byteLength": len(output),
+                "digest": _digest(output),
+                "path": "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl",
+            },
+            "package": "rulespec-conformance",
+            "packageVersion": VERSION,
+            "resources": source_rows,
+        }
+    )
+    return output, lock
+
+
+def _check(path: Path, expected: bytes) -> bool:
+    if not path.is_file():
+        print(f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} is missing")
+        return False
+    observed = path.read_bytes()
+    if observed != expected:
+        print(
+            f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} differs "
+            f"(expected {_digest(expected)}, found {_digest(observed)})"
+        )
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--check",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="refuse stale generated data instead of refreshing it",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    output, lock = render()
+    if args.check:
+        return 0 if _check(OUTPUT_PATH, output) and _check(LOCK_PATH, lock) else 1
+    OUTPUT_PATH.write_bytes(output)
+    LOCK_PATH.write_bytes(lock)
+    print(
+        "refreshed "
+        f"{OUTPUT_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} ({_digest(output)}) and "
+        f"{LOCK_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)}"
+    )
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Differential oracle for compiler-emitted adjudication SHACL-SPARQL.
+
+The Python implementation below is copied and reduced from the four relevant
+parts of ``bindings/atlas/3.1/tools/validate.py``. It deliberately imports
+neither that module nor RuleSpec compiler code: importing the implementation
+being replaced would make agreement circular.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import resource
+import sys
+import time
+from itertools import combinations
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from pyshacl import validate as shacl_validate
+from rdflib import Dataset, Graph, Literal, Namespace, URIRef
+from rdflib.namespace import RDF, SH, SKOS
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+BINDING = ROOT / "bindings/atlas/3.1"
+FIXTURES = BINDING / "fixtures"
+SHAPES_PATH = BINDING / "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"
+
+RKAF = Namespace("https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#")
+CASE = Namespace("urn:ref:move2-oracle:")
+
+RULE_SHAPES = {
+    "independence": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationFiveAxisIndependenceShape,
+    "complete-support": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationCompleteSupportShape,
+    "verdict-lattice": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationVerdictLatticeFoldShape,
+    "proof-replay": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationProofReplayShape,
+}
+
+CORPUS_EXPECTED = {
+    "adjudication-single-proof": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-validator-actor": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-independence-group": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-provider": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-provider-model": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-response-artifact": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-discarded-support": {"complete-support"},
+    "adjudication-relation-not-licensed": {"verdict-lattice"},
+    "adjudication-verdicts-disagree": {"verdict-lattice"},
+    "adjudication-foreign-comparison": {"proof-replay"},
+    "all-resource-profiles": set(),
+    "qualified-three-machine-support": set(),
+    "qualified-lattice-branches": set(),
+    "adjudication-refused-comparison-record": set(),
+}
+
+
+def _one(graph: Graph, subject: URIRef, predicate: URIRef) -> object:
+    values = list(graph.objects(subject, predicate))
+    if len(values) != 1:
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"oracle input requires one {predicate} on {subject}; found {len(values)}"
+        )
+    return values[0]
+
+
+def _fold_verdicts(verdicts: frozenset[object]) -> URIRef | None:
+    """Copied oracle for validate.py::_adjudicated_relation."""
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictSame}:
+        return SKOS.exactMatch
+    if verdicts <= {RKAF.verdictSame, RKAF.verdictNearSame} and (
+        RKAF.verdictNearSame in verdicts
+    ):
+        return SKOS.closeMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetBroader}:
+        return SKOS.broadMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower}:
+        return SKOS.narrowMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictRelated}:
+        return SKOS.relatedMatch
+    return None
+
+
+def python_oracle(graph: Graph) -> set[str]:
+    """Verdicts from the copied old Python behavior for the four rules."""
+    violations: set[str] = set()
+    comparisons = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    proofs = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.ResolverProofRecord))
+
+    for proof in proofs:
+        comparison = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofComparisonContext)
+        if proof not in set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord)):
+            violations.add("complete-support")
+        citing = {
+            subject
+            for subject in graph.subjects(RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, proof)
+            if subject in comparisons
+        }
+        if len(citing) > 1:
+            violations.add("proof-replay")
+
+    for comparison in comparisons:
+        if _one(graph, comparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome) != RKAF.comparisonSatisfied:
+            continue
+        cited = set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord))
+        facts: list[tuple[object, ...]] = []
+        for proof in cited:
+            issuer = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofIssuer)
+            lineage = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.hasAILineage)
+            facts.append(
+                (
+                    issuer,
+                    _one(graph, proof, RKAF.independenceGroup),
+                    _one(graph, issuer, RKAF.proofResolver),
+                    str(_one(graph, lineage, RKAF.modelId)),
+                    _one(graph, proof, RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact),
+                )
+            )
+        if not any(
+            all(left[index] != right[index] for index in range(5))
+            for left, right in combinations(facts, 2)
+        ):
+            violations.add("independence")
+
+        assertion = _one(graph, comparison, RKAF.comparisonExpectedAssertion)
+        stated_relation = _one(graph, assertion, RDF.predicate)
+        verdicts = frozenset(
+            _one(graph, proof, RKAF.adjudicationVerdict) for proof in cited
+        )
+        if _fold_verdicts(verdicts) != stated_relation:
+            violations.add("verdict-lattice")
+    return violations
+
+
+def shape_oracle(graph: Graph) -> set[str]:
+    """Run each emitted rule alone so its Boolean verdict has a stable ID."""
+    all_shapes = Graph().parse(SHAPES_PATH, format="turtle")
+    target_predicates = (
+        SH.targetClass,
+        SH.targetNode,
+        SH.targetSubjectsOf,
+        SH.targetObjectsOf,
+    )
+    violations: set[str] = set()
+    for rule, keep in RULE_SHAPES.items():
+        shapes = Graph()
+        for triple in all_shapes:
+            shapes.add(triple)
+        for predicate in target_predicates:
+            for subject, obj in list(shapes.subject_objects(predicate)):
+                if subject != keep:
+                    shapes.remove((subject, predicate, obj))
+        conforms, _, _ = shacl_validate(
+            graph,
+            shacl_graph=shapes,
+            inference="none",
+            advanced=True,
+            inplace=False,
+            abort_on_first=False,
+            meta_shacl=False,
+        )
+        if not conforms:
+            violations.add(rule)
+    return violations
+
+
+def _fixture_path(case_id: str) -> Path:
+    corpus = json.loads((FIXTURES / "corpus.json").read_bytes())
+    row = next(row for row in corpus["cases"] if row["id"] == case_id)
+    return FIXTURES / row["path"]
+
+
+def _fixture_graph(case_id: str) -> Graph:
+    root = _fixture_path(case_id)
+    if not root.is_dir():
+        raise SystemExit(
+            f"fixture {case_id} is not built; run "
+            "bindings/atlas/3.1/tools/build_fixtures.py first"
+        )
+    manifest = json.loads((root / "atlas-manifest.json").read_bytes())
+    asserted_id = URIRef(
+        next(row["id"] for row in manifest["graphs"] if row["role"] == "asserted")
+    )
+    dataset = Dataset()
+    for pack in manifest["packs"]:
+        payload = (root / pack["path"]).read_bytes()
+        if pack["transport"]["compression"] == "zstd":
+            try:
+                from compression import zstd
+            except ImportError:
+                from backports import zstd
+            payload = zstd.decompress(payload)
+        dataset.parse(data=payload.decode("utf-8"), format="nquads")
+    source = dataset.graph(asserted_id)
+    graph = Graph()
+    for triple in source:
+        graph.add(triple)
+    return graph
+
+
+def _add_proof(graph: Graph, key: str, *, cite: bool = True) -> URIRef:
+    proof = CASE[f"proof-{key}"]
+    issuer = CASE[f"issuer-{key}"]
+    lineage = CASE[f"lineage-{key}"]
+    graph.add((proof, RDF.type, RKAF.ResolverProofRecord))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.proofComparisonContext, CASE.comparison))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.proofIssuer, issuer))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.independenceGroup, CASE[f"group-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.hasAILineage, lineage))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact, CASE[f"response-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.adjudicationVerdict, RKAF.verdictSame))
+    graph.add((issuer, RKAF.proofResolver, CASE[f"provider-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((lineage, RKAF.modelId, Literal(f"model-{key}")))
+    if cite:
+        graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, proof))
+    return proof
+
+
+def _base_graph() -> Graph:
+    graph = Graph()
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome, RKAF.comparisonSatisfied))
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonExpectedAssertion, CASE.assertion))
+    graph.add((CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.exactMatch))
+    _add_proof(graph, "alpha")
+    _add_proof(graph, "beta")
+    return graph
+
+
+def _clone(graph: Graph) -> Graph:
+    result = Graph()
+    for triple in graph:
+        result.add(triple)
+    return result
+
+
+def _replace(graph: Graph, subject: URIRef, predicate: URIRef, value: object) -> None:
+    graph.remove((subject, predicate, None))
+    graph.add((subject, predicate, value))
+
+
+def mutation_cases() -> dict[str, tuple[Graph, set[str]]]:
+    base = _base_graph()
+    cases: dict[str, tuple[Graph, set[str]]] = {"valid-exact": (base, set())}
+
+    single = _clone(base)
+    single.remove((CASE["proof-beta"], None, None))
+    single.remove((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, CASE["proof-beta"]))
+    cases["single-proof"] = (single, {"independence"})
+
+    axis_changes = {
+        "same-actor": (CASE["proof-beta"], RKAF.proofIssuer, CASE["issuer-alpha"]),
+        "same-group": (
+            CASE["proof-beta"],
+            RKAF.independenceGroup,
+            CASE["group-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-response": (
+            CASE["proof-beta"],
+            RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact,
+            CASE["response-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-provider": (
+            CASE["issuer-beta"],
+            RKAF.proofResolver,
+            CASE["provider-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-model": (
+            CASE["lineage-beta"],
+            RKAF.modelId,
+            Literal("model-alpha"),
+        ),
+    }
+    for name, (subject, predicate, value) in axis_changes.items():
+        graph = _clone(base)
+        _replace(graph, subject, predicate, value)
+        cases[name] = (graph, {"independence"})
+
+    discarded = _clone(base)
+    _add_proof(discarded, "gamma", cite=False)
+    cases["discarded-support"] = (discarded, {"complete-support"})
+
+    replay = _clone(base)
+    replay.add((CASE.otherComparison, RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    replay.add((CASE.otherComparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome, RKAF.comparisonRefused))
+    replay.add(
+        (CASE.otherComparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, CASE["proof-alpha"])
+    )
+    cases["proof-replay"] = (replay, {"proof-replay"})
+
+    mixed_exact = _clone(base)
+    _replace(
+        mixed_exact,
+        CASE["proof-beta"],
+        RKAF.adjudicationVerdict,
+        RKAF.verdictNearSame,
+    )
+    cases["exact-with-near"] = (mixed_exact, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    valid_close = _clone(mixed_exact)
+    _replace(valid_close, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.closeMatch)
+    cases["valid-close"] = (valid_close, set())
+
+    close_without_near = _clone(base)
+    _replace(close_without_near, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.closeMatch)
+    cases["close-without-near"] = (close_without_near, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    branches = (
+        ("valid-broad", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetBroader, set()),
+        ("valid-narrow", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower, set()),
+        ("valid-related", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictRelated, set()),
+        ("broad-with-same", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+        ("narrow-with-same", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+        ("related-with-same", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+    )
+    for name, relation, verdict, expected in branches:
+        graph = _clone(base)
+        _replace(graph, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, relation)
+        for key in ("alpha", "beta"):
+            _replace(
+                graph,
+                CASE[f"proof-{key}"],
+                RKAF.adjudicationVerdict,
+                verdict,
+            )
+        cases[name] = (graph, expected)
+
+    unknown = _clone(base)
+    _replace(unknown, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, CASE.unsupportedRelation)
+    cases["unsupported-relation"] = (unknown, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    refused = _clone(mixed_exact)
+    _replace(
+        refused,
+        CASE.comparison,
+        RKAF.comparisonOutcome,
+        RKAF.comparisonRefused,
+    )
+    cases["refused-does-not-fold"] = (refused, set())
+    return cases
+
+
+def _run_case(kind: str, case_id: str, graph: Graph, expected: set[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
+    python = python_oracle(graph)
+    shacl = shape_oracle(graph)
+    if python != shacl or python != expected:
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"{kind}/{case_id}: expected={sorted(expected)}, "
+            f"python={sorted(python)}, shacl={sorted(shacl)}"
+        )
+    return {
+        "expected": sorted(expected),
+        "id": case_id,
+        "kind": kind,
+        "python": sorted(python),
+        "shacl": sorted(shacl),
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output",
+        type=Path,
+        default=ROOT / "research/move2/measurements.json",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    started = time.perf_counter()
+    results = [
+        _run_case("corpus", case_id, _fixture_graph(case_id), expected)
+        for case_id, expected in CORPUS_EXPECTED.items()
+    ]
+    results.extend(
+        _run_case("mutation", case_id, graph, expected)
+        for case_id, (graph, expected) in mutation_cases().items()
+    )
+    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
+    peak = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
+    peak_mib = peak / (1024 * 1024) if sys.platform == "darwin" else peak / 1024
+    summary = {
+        "corpusCases": sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
+        "corpusRuleChecks": 4 * sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
+        "elapsedSeconds": round(elapsed, 3),
+        "engine": "pySHACL 0.31.0",
+        "mutationCases": sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
+        "mutationRuleChecks": 4
+        * sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
+        "peakRssMiB": round(peak_mib, 1),
+        "results": results,
+        "status": "PASS",
+    }
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+    print(
+        f"move-2 oracle PASS: {summary['corpusCases']} corpus + "
+        f"{summary['mutationCases']} mutation cases in {summary['elapsedSeconds']}s; "
+        f"peak RSS {summary['peakRssMiB']} MiB"
+    )
+    return 0
+

+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

   281	    r'(?ms)^#(?P<shape>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*Shape)Sparql:\s*"""\n'
   282	    r'(?P<body>.*?)\n"""\s*$'

   289	def parse_shacl_sparql_annotations(source: str) -> list[SparqlConstraintDef]:
   290	    """Parse the fail-closed CUE annotation format for graph rules.
   291	
   292	    The definition name supplies the stable shape local name. Its multiline
   293	    string has a generated-scaffolding header, a literal ``---`` separator,
   294	    then the SPARQL SELECT query::
   295	
   296	        #ExampleShapeSparql: <CUE multiline string>
   297	          targetClass: rkaf:Example
   298	          message: Explanation shown in a SHACL result.
   299	          ---
   300	          PREFIX rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#>
   301	          SELECT $this WHERE { ... }
   302	
   303	    Repeating ``targetClass`` is allowed. Everything else is rejected rather
   304	    than silently omitted from the emitted constraint.
   305	    """
   306	
   307	    constraints: list[SparqlConstraintDef] = []
   308	    seen: set[str] = set()
   309	    for match in SHACL_SPARQL_BLOCK_RE.finditer(source):
   310	        shape_name = match.group("shape")
   311	        if shape_name in seen:
   312	            raise CompileError(f"duplicate SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name}")
   313	        seen.add(shape_name)
   314	        header, separator, select = match.group("body").partition("\n---\n")
   315	        if not separator:
   316	            raise CompileError(
   317	                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no --- query separator"
   318	            )
   319	        targets: list[str] = []
   320	        message: Optional[str] = None
   321	        for raw_line in header.splitlines():
   322	            line = raw_line.strip()
   323	            if not line:
   324	                continue
   325	            key, colon, value = line.partition(":")
   326	            if not colon or not value.strip():
   327	                raise CompileError(
   328	                    f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has malformed header {line!r}"
   329	                )
   330	            value = value.strip()
   331	            if key == "targetClass":
   332	                if not COMPACT_OR_ABSOLUTE_IRI_RE.fullmatch(value):
   333	                    raise CompileError(
   334	                        f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has invalid targetClass {value!r}"
   335	                    )
   336	                targets.append(value)
   337	            elif key == "message":
   338	                if message is not None:
   339	                    raise CompileError(
   340	                        f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} repeats message"
   341	                    )
   342	                message = value
   343	            else:
   344	                raise CompileError(
   345	                    f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has unknown header {key!r}"
   346	                )
   347	        query = select.strip()
   348	        if not targets:
   349	            raise CompileError(
   350	                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no targetClass"
   351	            )
   352	        if not message:
   353	            raise CompileError(f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no message")
   354	        if not re.search(r"(?i)\bSELECT\s+(?:DISTINCT\s+)?\$this\b", query):
   355	            raise CompileError(
   356	                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} must SELECT $this"
   357	            )
   358	        if '"""' in query:
   359	            raise CompileError(
   360	                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} contains a Turtle long-string terminator"
   361	            )
   362	        constraints.append(
   363	            SparqlConstraintDef(
   364	                shape_name=shape_name,
   365	                target_classes=targets,
   366	                message=message,
   367	                select=query,
   368	            )
   369	        )
   370	    return constraints

   374	    """Parse one CUE constraint file into the projector's flat AST.
   375

   386	    )
   387	
   388	    # Pre-pass: join any line that ends with `|` into the next line (CUE
   389	    # disjunction continuation). This works for both top-level enum unions and
   390	    # in-shape property assignments whose RHS spans multiple lines.
  3700	            for br in disj:

  3702	                    bp = br.properties[0]
  3703	                    out.append(f"    [ sh:property [ sh:path {bp.name} ; sh:minCount 1 ] ]")

  3705	        out.append("  .")
  3706	        out.append("")

  3741	            )

    36	#: never a guess: `json_schema("rulemaking", family="profiles/us-rulemaking")`.
    37	COMPILED_TARGETS: tuple[str, ...] = (

    48	def _segments(*parts: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    49	    """Split `parts` into path segments, refusing anything that walks out.
    50	
    51	    The packaged data is a closed set. `..` or an absolute segment would leave
    52	    it, and on a zip-imported package it would not resolve at all, so it is a
    53	    caller error rather than a lookup that happens to work in a checkout.
    54	    """
    55	    segments: list[str] = []
    56	    for part in parts:
    57	        text = str(part)
    58	        if text.startswith("/"):
    59	            raise ValueError(f"resource path is absolute: {part!r}")
    60	        for segment in text.split("/"):
    61	            if not segment or segment == ".":
    62	                continue
    63	            if segment == "..":
    64	                raise ValueError(f"resource path escapes the packaged data: {part!r}")
    65	            segments.append(segment)
    66	    if not segments:
    67	        raise ValueError("no resource path given")
    68	    return tuple(segments)
    69	
    70	
    71	def resource(*parts: str) -> Traversable:
    72	    """The `Traversable` for a packaged file, whether or not it exists."""
    73	    target = DATA_ROOT
    74	    for segment in _segments(*parts):
    75	        target = target / segment
    76	    return target
    77	
    78	
    79	def _require(*parts: str) -> Traversable:
    80	    target = resource(*parts)
    81	    if not target.is_file():
    82	        raise FileNotFoundError(
    83	            f"{'/'.join(_segments(*parts))} is not packaged with this "
    84	            f"Rulespec contract (data root: {DATA_ROOT})"
    85	        )
    86	    return target
    87

    89	def read_text(*parts: str) -> str:
    90	    """The UTF-8 text of a packaged file."""
    91	    return _require(*parts).read_text(encoding="utf-8")

   103	        sorted(
   104	            entry.name[: -len(suffix)]

   153

   155	    what CUE can express, and `shapes/` carries the Pattern C conditionals and
   156	    cross-node constraints it cannot. A consumer validating rkaf data loads
   157	    both.
   158	    """
   159	    return read_text("shapes", f"{name}.ttl")

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Refresh the RuleSpec-owned adjudication shapes vendored into this binding.
     3	
     4	The binding validator deliberately imports no RefSpec or RuleSpec package
     5	code. This development-time generator is the only package-aware side of that
     6	boundary: it reads compiler output through the installed
     7	``rulespec_conformance.contract.resources`` accessor, writes plain Turtle
     8	beside the Atlas shapes, and records exact source and output digests.

    18	from rulespec_conformance.contract import VERSION, resources

    20	BINDING_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    21	OUTPUT_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"
    22	LOCK_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.lock.json"

    26	def _digest(payload: bytes) -> str:
    27	    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
    28	
    29	
    30	def _canonical_json(value: object) -> bytes:
    31	    return (
    32	        json.dumps(
    33	            value,
    34	            ensure_ascii=False,
    35	            allow_nan=False,
    36	            sort_keys=True,
    37	            separators=(",", ":"),
    38	        ).encode("utf-8")
    39	        + b"\n"
    40	    )
    41	
    42	
    43	def render() -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
    44	    parts = [
    45	        "# GENERATED by tools/refresh_rulespec_adjudication_shapes.py.",
    46	        "# Source: rulespec-conformance compiler output; do not edit here.",
    47	        f"# Rulespec contract version: {VERSION}",
    48	        "",
    49	    ]
    50	    source_rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    51	    for name in RESOURCE_NAMES:
    52	        text = resources.shacl_sparql(name, family="analysis")
    53	        payload = text.encode("utf-8")
    54	        source_rows.append(
    55	            {
    56	                "accessor": (
    57	                    "rulespec_conformance.contract.resources."
    58	                    f"shacl_sparql({name!r}, family='analysis')"
    59	                ),
    60	                "byteLength": len(payload),
    61	                "digest": _digest(payload),
    62	                "name": name,
    63	            }
    64	        )
    65	        parts.extend((text.rstrip(), ""))
    66	    output = "\n".join(parts).encode("utf-8")
    67	    lock = _canonical_json(
    68	        {
    69	            "format": "RulespecAdjudicationShapeLock",
    70	            "formatVersion": "1.0",
    71	            "output": {
    72	                "byteLength": len(output),
    73	                "digest": _digest(output),
    74	                "path": "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl",
    75	            },
    76	            "package": "rulespec-conformance",
    77	            "packageVersion": VERSION,
    78	            "resources": source_rows,
    79	        }
    80	    )
    81	    return output, lock
    82	
    83	
    84	def _check(path: Path, expected: bytes) -> bool:
    85	    if not path.is_file():
    86	        print(f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} is missing")
    87	        return False
    88	    observed = path.read_bytes()
    89	    if observed != expected:
    90	        print(
    91	            f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} differs "
    92	            f"(expected {_digest(expected)}, found {_digest(observed)})"
    93	        )
    94	        return False
    95	    return True
    96	
    97	
    98	def main() -> int:
    99	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
   100	    parser.add_argument(
   101	        "--check",
   102	        action="store_true",
   103	        help="refuse stale generated data instead of refreshing it",
   104	    )
   105	    args = parser.parse_args()
   106	    output, lock = render()
   107	    if args.check:
   108	        return 0 if _check(OUTPUT_PATH, output) and _check(LOCK_PATH, lock) else 1
   109	    OUTPUT_PATH.write_bytes(output)
   110	    LOCK_PATH.write_bytes(lock)
   111	    print(
   112	        "refreshed "
   113	        f"{OUTPUT_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} ({_digest(output)}) and "
   114	        f"{LOCK_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)}"
   115	    )
   116	    return 0
   117

   119	if __name__ == "__main__":
   120	    raise SystemExit(main())

   104	# The semantic contract: the RULES a distribution is validated *against*.
   105	# Changing any of these changes what conformance means, so every fixture must
   106	# be reissued against the new meaning -- that is the point of pinning them into
   107	# each manifest and acceptance record as `contractDigest`.
   108	#
   109	# `fixtures/corpus.json` is deliberately NOT here, and that is the whole
   110	# distinction this list now draws. The corpus is the PROOF that this validator
   111	# behaves as the rules say; it is not one of the rules. While it sat in this
   112	# list, adding a single conformance case moved the contract digest, which moved
   113	# every manifest, acceptance record and construction summary on disk, which
   114	# broke the external manifest pins and invalidated a signed release -- for a
   115	# contract that had not moved a byte. Proof identity lives where the proof is
   116	# described instead: `corpus_digest()` is recorded in each acceptance record,
   117	# beside the validator identity it qualifies. See REF-029.
   118	CONTRACT_PATHS = (

   129	# The programs that read that contract, and the versions they run against.
   130	# These decide the exact bytes the builder emits, which is why the fixture
   131	# receipt hashes them, but they do not decide what conformance *means* -- and
   132	# which validator produced a verdict is already declared, by name and number,
   133	# through VALIDATOR_ID/VALIDATOR_VERSION in every manifest and acceptance
   134	# record and checked by _check_binding_pins. Folding their source into
   135	# contractDigest said the same thing a second way and made every edit to
   136	# a tool reissue the whole corpus for a contract that had not moved. README.md
   137	# is in neither list: it is prose, and prose settles nothing.
   138	#
   139	# Conformance identity must not move when a program changes, but a *cached
   140	# verdict* is only as good as the program that computed it: a new refusal added
   141	# here would otherwise be answered from a receipt the old validator wrote, and
   142	# the cache returns before the procedural checks ever run. So the validation
   143	# cache key covers this list and the runtime below as well as the contract --
   144	# identity is contract-only, cache validity is contract plus tools.

  1954	    """Digest the conformance corpus that proves this validator's behaviour.
  1955	
  1956	    Proof identity, not contract identity. An acceptance record says which
  1957	    validator ran; this says which corpus that validator was answerable to when
  1958	    it ran. It is RECORDED into the acceptance record and deliberately not
  1959	    re-derived by `_check_binding_pins`: growing the corpus must leave every
  1960	    artifact on disk valid, because nothing a new test case says changes what

  2691	    for pack in manifest["packs"]:
  2692	        if pack["graphCounts"]["projection"] or pack["graphCounts"]["derived"]:
  2693	            continue
  2694	        pack_id = pack["packId"]
  2695	        declared = set(pack["dependencies"])
  2696	        if declared != expected[pack_id]:
  2697	            _fail(
  2698	                "pack.dependency",
  2699	                f"{pack_id} dependencies differ; "
  2700	                f"missing={sorted(expected[pack_id] - declared)}, "
  2701	                f"extra={sorted(declared - expected[pack_id])}",
  2702	            )

  3654	def _run_shacl(graphs: Mapping[str, Graph], ontology: Graph, shapes: Graph) -> None:
  3655	    """Validate authoritative inputs; exact regeneration validates the projection.
  3656	
  3657	    Red builds fail fast. Measured on a 32M-quad non-conforming distribution
  3658	    (2026-08-11, `plans/validation-cost-reset-plan.md`), the batched fast path
  3659	    detected the miss in minutes and the whole-graph normative run then took
  3660	    **94 minutes solely to phrase the failure report** -- 78% of a two-hour
  3661	    run, on the path a developer iterates on. So the default red path
  3662	    re-validates only the focus nodes the fast path already named, under the
  3663	    unmodified normative shapes over the unmodified data graph
  3664	    (`_focused_shacl_report`): the same engine, the same constraint
  3665	    components, seconds instead of hours.
  3666	
  3667	    `REFSPEC_ATLAS_VALIDATION_MODE=audit` restores the whole-graph normative
  3668	    run -- read once, here, so one distribution is never validated half in
  3669	    each mode. Anything else, including unset, fails fast. The failure code is
  3670	    `shacl.data` and the message names every violated constraint component in
  3671	    both modes; the focused path only narrows which nodes the engine is asked
  3672	    about, and falls back to the whole-graph report whenever the sample cannot
  3673	    be trusted to reproduce the same components.

    57	def _one(graph: Graph, subject: URIRef, predicate: URIRef) -> object:
    58	    values = list(graph.objects(subject, predicate))
    59	    if len(values) != 1:
    60	        raise AssertionError(
    61	            f"oracle input requires one {predicate} on {subject}; found {len(values)}"
    62	        )
    63	    return values[0]

    66	def _fold_verdicts(verdicts: frozenset[object]) -> URIRef | None:
    67	    """Copied oracle for validate.py::_adjudicated_relation."""
    68	    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictSame}:
    69	        return SKOS.exactMatch
    70	    if verdicts <= {RKAF.verdictSame, RKAF.verdictNearSame} and (
    71	        RKAF.verdictNearSame in verdicts
    72	    ):
    73	        return SKOS.closeMatch
    74	    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetBroader}:
    75	        return SKOS.broadMatch
    76	    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower}:
    77	        return SKOS.narrowMatch
    78	    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictRelated}:
    79	        return SKOS.relatedMatch
    80	    return None

    83	def python_oracle(graph: Graph) -> set[str]:
    84	    """Verdicts from the copied old Python behavior for the four rules."""
    85	    violations: set[str] = set()
    86	    comparisons = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
    87	    proofs = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.ResolverProofRecord))
    88	
    89	    for proof in proofs:
    90	        comparison = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofComparisonContext)
    91	        if proof not in set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord)):
    92	            violations.add("complete-support")
    93	        citing = {
    94	            subject
    95	            for subject in graph.subjects(RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, proof)
    96	            if subject in comparisons
    97	        }
    98	        if len(citing) > 1:
    99	            violations.add("proof-replay")
   100	
   101	    for comparison in comparisons:
   102	        if _one(graph, comparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome) != RKAF.comparisonSatisfied:
   103	            continue
   104	        cited = set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord))
   105	        facts: list[tuple[object, ...]] = []
   106	        for proof in cited:
   107	            issuer = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofIssuer)
   108	            lineage = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.hasAILineage)
   109	            facts.append(
   110	                (
   111	                    issuer,
   112	                    _one(graph, proof, RKAF.independenceGroup),
   113	                    _one(graph, issuer, RKAF.proofResolver),
   114	                    str(_one(graph, lineage, RKAF.modelId)),

   302	
   303	    close_without_near = _clone(base)
   304	    _replace(close_without_near, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.closeMatch)
   305	    cases["close-without-near"] = (close_without_near, {"verdict-lattice"})
   306	
   307	    branches = (
   308	        ("valid-broad", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetBroader, set()),
   309	        ("valid-narrow", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower, set()),
   310	        ("valid-related", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictRelated, set()),
   311	        ("broad-with-same", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
   312	        ("narrow-with-same", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
   313	        ("related-with-same", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
   314	    )
   315	    for name, relation, verdict, expected in branches:
   316	        graph = _clone(base)
   317	        _replace(graph, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, relation)
   318	        for key in ("alpha", "beta"):
   319	            _replace(
   320	                graph,
   321	                CASE[f"proof-{key}"],
   322	                RKAF.adjudicationVerdict,
   323	                verdict,
   324	            )
   325	        cases[name] = (graph, expected)
   326	
   327	    unknown = _clone(base)
   328	    _replace(unknown, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, CASE.unsupportedRelation)
   329	    cases["unsupported-relation"] = (unknown, {"verdict-lattice"})
   330	
   331	    refused = _clone(mixed_exact)
   332	    _replace(
   333	        refused,
   334	        CASE.comparison,
   335	        RKAF.comparisonOutcome,
   336	        RKAF.comparisonRefused,
   337	    )
   338	    cases["refused-does-not-fold"] = (refused, set())
   339	    return cases
   340	
   341	
   342	def _run_case(kind: str, case_id: str, graph: Graph, expected: set[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
   343	    python = python_oracle(graph)
   344	    shacl = shape_oracle(graph)
   345	    if python != shacl or python != expected:
   346	        raise AssertionError(
   347	            f"{kind}/{case_id}: expected={sorted(expected)}, "
   348	            f"python={sorted(python)}, shacl={sorted(shacl)}"
   349	        )
   350	    return {
   351	        "expected": sorted(expected),
   352	        "id": case_id,
   353	        "kind": kind,
   354	        "python": sorted(python),
   355	        "shacl": sorted(shacl),
   356	    }
   357	
   358	
   359	def main() -> int:
   360	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
   361	    parser.add_argument(
   362	        "--output",
   363	        type=Path,
   364	        default=ROOT / "research/move2/measurements.json",
   365	    )
   366	    args = parser.parse_args()
   367	    started = time.perf_counter()
   368	    results = [
   369	        _run_case("corpus", case_id, _fixture_graph(case_id), expected)
   370	        for case_id, expected in CORPUS_EXPECTED.items()
   371	    ]
   372	    results.extend(
   373	        _run_case("mutation", case_id, graph, expected)
   374	        for case_id, (graph, expected) in mutation_cases().items()
   375	    )
   376	    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
   377	    peak = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
   378	    peak_mib = peak / (1024 * 1024) if sys.platform == "darwin" else peak / 1024
   379	    summary = {
   380	        "corpusCases": sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
   381	        "corpusRuleChecks": 4 * sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
   382	        "elapsedSeconds": round(elapsed, 3),
   383	        "engine": "pySHACL 0.31.0",
   384	        "mutationCases": sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
   385	        "mutationRuleChecks": 4
   386	        * sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
   387	        "peakRssMiB": round(peak_mib, 1),
   388	        "results": results,
   389	        "status": "PASS",
   390	    }
   391	    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   392	    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
   393	    print(
   394	        f"move-2 oracle PASS: {summary['corpusCases']} corpus + "
   395	        f"{summary['mutationCases']} mutation cases in {summary['elapsedSeconds']}s; "
   396	        f"peak RSS {summary['peakRssMiB']} MiB"
   397	    )
   398	    return 0
   399	
   400	
   401	if __name__ == "__main__":
   402	    raise SystemExit(main())

+SHACL_SPARQL_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(
+    r'(?ms)^#(?P<shape>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*Shape)Sparql:\s*"""\n'
+    r'(?P<body>.*?)\n"""\s*$'
+)
+COMPACT_OR_ABSOLUTE_IRI_RE = re.compile(
+    r"^(?:[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:[^\s]+|<[^\s<>]+>)$"
+)
+
+
+def parse_shacl_sparql_annotations(source: str) -> list[SparqlConstraintDef]:
+    """Parse the fail-closed CUE annotation format for graph rules.
+
+    The definition name supplies the stable shape local name. Its multiline
+    string has a generated-scaffolding header, a literal ``---`` separator,
+    then the SPARQL SELECT query::
+
+        #ExampleShapeSparql: <CUE multiline string>
+          targetClass: rkaf:Example
+          message: Explanation shown in a SHACL result.
+          ---
+          PREFIX rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#>
+          SELECT $this WHERE { ... }
+
+    Repeating ``targetClass`` is allowed. Everything else is rejected rather
+    than silently omitted from the emitted constraint.
+    """
+
+    constraints: list[SparqlConstraintDef] = []
+    seen: set[str] = set()
+    for match in SHACL_SPARQL_BLOCK_RE.finditer(source):
+        shape_name = match.group("shape")
+        if shape_name in seen:
+            raise CompileError(f"duplicate SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name}")
+        seen.add(shape_name)
+        header, separator, select = match.group("body").partition("\n---\n")
+        if not separator:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no --- query separator"
+            )
+        targets: list[str] = []
+        message: Optional[str] = None
+        for raw_line in header.splitlines():
+            line = raw_line.strip()
+            if not line:
+                continue
+            key, colon, value = line.partition(":")
+            if not colon or not value.strip():
+                raise CompileError(
+                    f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has malformed header {line!r}"
+                )
+            value = value.strip()
+            if key == "targetClass":
+                if not COMPACT_OR_ABSOLUTE_IRI_RE.fullmatch(value):
+                    raise CompileError(
+                        f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has invalid targetClass {value!r}"
+                    )
+                targets.append(value)
+            elif key == "message":
+                if message is not None:
+                    raise CompileError(
+                        f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} repeats message"
+                    )
+                message = value
+            else:
+                raise CompileError(
+                    f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has unknown header {key!r}"
+                )
+        query = select.strip()
+        if not targets:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no targetClass"
+            )
+        if not message:
+            raise CompileError(f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no message")
+        if not re.search(r"(?i)\bSELECT\s+(?:DISTINCT\s+)?\$this\b", query):
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} must SELECT $this"
+            )
+        if '"""' in query:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} contains a Turtle long-string terminator"
+            )
+        constraints.append(
+            SparqlConstraintDef(
+                shape_name=shape_name,
+                target_classes=targets,
+                message=message,
+                select=query,
+            )
+        )
+    return constraints
+

+# ---- SHACL-SPARQL target (annotated relational rules) --------------------
+
+def target_shacl_sparql(doc: ConstraintDoc) -> str:
+    """Emit only the relational rules explicitly carried by this CUE file."""
+
+    out: list[str] = [
+        "# AUTO-GENERATED by tools/constraints_compile.py "
+        "(target=shacl-sparql).",
+        "# Source: " + (
+            _source_relpath(doc.source_file) or str(doc.source_file or "unknown")
+        ),
+        "# DO NOT EDIT: change the #*ShapeSparql annotation in the CUE source.",
+        "",
+        "@prefix sh:   <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .",
+        "@prefix rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#> .",
+        "",
+    ]
+    for constraint in doc.sparql_constraints:
+        out.append(f"rkaf:{constraint.shape_name} a sh:NodeShape ;")
+        for target_class in constraint.target_classes:
+            out.append(f"  sh:targetClass {target_class} ;")
+        out.extend(
+            (
+                "  sh:sparql [",
+                "    a sh:SPARQLConstraint ;",
+                f"    sh:message {json.dumps(constraint.message)} ;",
+                '    sh:select """',
+                constraint.select,
+                '    """ ;',
+                "  ] .",
+                "",
+            )
+        )
+    return "\n".join(out)

+                "MachineAdjudicationCompleteSupportShape",
+                "MachineAdjudicationVerdictLatticeFoldShape",
+                "MachineAdjudicationProofReplayShape",
+            )

+Four relational adjudication rules are generated by the RuleSpec CUE
+compiler. They reach this copy-and-run binding as plain data in
+`shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl`; the validator still imports no

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Refresh the RuleSpec-owned adjudication shapes vendored into this binding.
+
+The binding validator deliberately imports no RefSpec or RuleSpec package
+code. This development-time generator is the only package-aware side of that
+boundary: it reads compiler output through the installed
+``rulespec_conformance.contract.resources`` accessor, writes plain Turtle
+beside the Atlas shapes, and records exact source and output digests.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from rulespec_conformance.contract import VERSION, resources
+
+BINDING_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+OUTPUT_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"
+LOCK_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.lock.json"
+RESOURCE_NAMES = ("machine-adjudication", "resolver-proof-record")
+
+
+def _digest(payload: bytes) -> str:
+    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _canonical_json(value: object) -> bytes:
+    return (
+        json.dumps(
+            value,
+            ensure_ascii=False,
+            allow_nan=False,
+            sort_keys=True,
+            separators=(",", ":"),
+        ).encode("utf-8")
+        + b"\n"
+    )
+
+
+def render() -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
+    parts = [
+        "# GENERATED by tools/refresh_rulespec_adjudication_shapes.py.",
+        "# Source: rulespec-conformance compiler output; do not edit here.",
+        f"# Rulespec contract version: {VERSION}",
+        "",
+    ]
+    source_rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
+    for name in RESOURCE_NAMES:
+        text = resources.shacl_sparql(name, family="analysis")
+        payload = text.encode("utf-8")
+        source_rows.append(
+            {
+                "accessor": (
+                    "rulespec_conformance.contract.resources."
+                    f"shacl_sparql({name!r}, family='analysis')"
+                ),
+                "byteLength": len(payload),
+                "digest": _digest(payload),
+                "name": name,
+            }
+        )
+        parts.extend((text.rstrip(), ""))
+    output = "\n".join(parts).encode("utf-8")
+    lock = _canonical_json(
+        {
+            "format": "RulespecAdjudicationShapeLock",
+            "formatVersion": "1.0",
+            "output": {
+                "byteLength": len(output),
+                "digest": _digest(output),
+                "path": "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl",
+            },
+            "package": "rulespec-conformance",
+            "packageVersion": VERSION,
+            "resources": source_rows,
+        }
+    )
+    return output, lock
+
+
+def _check(path: Path, expected: bytes) -> bool:
+    if not path.is_file():
+        print(f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} is missing")
+        return False
+    observed = path.read_bytes()
+    if observed != expected:
+        print(
+            f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} differs "
+            f"(expected {_digest(expected)}, found {_digest(observed)})"
+        )
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--check",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="refuse stale generated data instead of refreshing it",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    output, lock = render()
+    if args.check:
+        return 0 if _check(OUTPUT_PATH, output) and _check(LOCK_PATH, lock) else 1
+    OUTPUT_PATH.write_bytes(output)
+    LOCK_PATH.write_bytes(lock)
+    print(
+        "refreshed "
+        f"{OUTPUT_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} ({_digest(output)}) and "
+        f"{LOCK_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)}"
+    )
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+def _check_rulespec_shapes_lock() -> None:
+    """Verify the local compiler output against its package-provenance pin."""
+
+    lock = _load_json(RULESPEC_SHAPES_LOCK_PATH, require_canonical=True)
+    if not isinstance(lock, Mapping) or set(lock) != {
+        "format",
+        "formatVersion",
+        "output",
+        "package",
+        "packageVersion",
+        "resources",
+    }:
+        _fail("binding.rulespec-shapes", "RuleSpec shape lock is malformed")
+    if (
+        lock["format"] != "RulespecAdjudicationShapeLock"
+        or lock["formatVersion"] != "1.0"
+        or lock["package"] != "rulespec-conformance"
+        or not isinstance(lock["packageVersion"], str)
+        or not lock["packageVersion"]
+    ):
+        _fail("binding.rulespec-shapes", "RuleSpec shape lock identity differs")
+    output = lock["output"]
+    payload = RULESPEC_SHAPES_PATH.read_bytes()
+    if output != {
+        "byteLength": len(payload),
+        "digest": "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest(),
+        "path": "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl",
+    }:
+        _fail("binding.rulespec-shapes", "RuleSpec shape output differs from its lock")
+    resources = lock["resources"]
+    if (
+        not isinstance(resources, list)
+        or [row.get("name") for row in resources if isinstance(row, Mapping)]
+        != ["machine-adjudication", "resolver-proof-record"]
+        or any(
+            not isinstance(row, Mapping)
+            or set(row) != {"accessor", "byteLength", "digest", "name"}
+            or not isinstance(row["byteLength"], int)
+            or row["byteLength"] <= 0
+            or not isinstance(row["digest"], str)
+            or not DIGEST_RE.fullmatch(row["digest"])
+            for row in resources
+        )
+    ):
+        _fail("binding.rulespec-shapes", "RuleSpec shape resource pins are malformed")
+

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Differential oracle for compiler-emitted adjudication SHACL-SPARQL.
+
+The Python implementation below is copied and reduced from the four relevant
+parts of ``bindings/atlas/3.1/tools/validate.py``. It deliberately imports
+neither that module nor RuleSpec compiler code: importing the implementation
+being replaced would make agreement circular.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import resource
+import sys
+import time
+from itertools import combinations
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from pyshacl import validate as shacl_validate
+from rdflib import Dataset, Graph, Literal, Namespace, URIRef
+from rdflib.namespace import RDF, SH, SKOS
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+BINDING = ROOT / "bindings/atlas/3.1"
+FIXTURES = BINDING / "fixtures"
+SHAPES_PATH = BINDING / "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"
+
+RKAF = Namespace("https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#")
+CASE = Namespace("urn:ref:move2-oracle:")
+
+RULE_SHAPES = {
+    "independence": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationFiveAxisIndependenceShape,
+    "complete-support": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationCompleteSupportShape,
+    "verdict-lattice": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationVerdictLatticeFoldShape,
+    "proof-replay": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationProofReplayShape,
+}
+
+CORPUS_EXPECTED = {
+    "adjudication-single-proof": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-validator-actor": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-independence-group": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-provider": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-provider-model": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-response-artifact": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-discarded-support": {"complete-support"},
+    "adjudication-relation-not-licensed": {"verdict-lattice"},
+    "adjudication-verdicts-disagree": {"verdict-lattice"},
+    "adjudication-foreign-comparison": {"proof-replay"},
+    "all-resource-profiles": set(),
+    "qualified-three-machine-support": set(),
+    "qualified-lattice-branches": set(),
+    "adjudication-refused-comparison-record": set(),
+}
+
+
+def _one(graph: Graph, subject: URIRef, predicate: URIRef) -> object:
+    values = list(graph.objects(subject, predicate))
+    if len(values) != 1:
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"oracle input requires one {predicate} on {subject}; found {len(values)}"
+        )
+    return values[0]
+
+
+def _fold_verdicts(verdicts: frozenset[object]) -> URIRef | None:
+    """Copied oracle for validate.py::_adjudicated_relation."""
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictSame}:
+        return SKOS.exactMatch
+    if verdicts <= {RKAF.verdictSame, RKAF.verdictNearSame} and (
+        RKAF.verdictNearSame in verdicts
+    ):
+        return SKOS.closeMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetBroader}:
+        return SKOS.broadMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower}:
+        return SKOS.narrowMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictRelated}:
+        return SKOS.relatedMatch
+    return None
+
+
+def python_oracle(graph: Graph) -> set[str]:
+    """Verdicts from the copied old Python behavior for the four rules."""
+    violations: set[str] = set()
+    comparisons = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    proofs = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.ResolverProofRecord))
+
+    for proof in proofs:
+        comparison = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofComparisonContext)
+        if proof not in set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord)):
+            violations.add("complete-support")
+        citing = {
+            subject
+            for subject in graph.subjects(RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, proof)
+            if subject in comparisons
+        }
+        if len(citing) > 1:
+            violations.add("proof-replay")
+
+    for comparison in comparisons:
+        if _one(graph, comparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome) != RKAF.comparisonSatisfied:
+            continue
+        cited = set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord))
+        facts: list[tuple[object, ...]] = []
+        for proof in cited:
+            issuer = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofIssuer)
+            lineage = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.hasAILineage)
+            facts.append(
+                (
+                    issuer,
+                    _one(graph, proof, RKAF.independenceGroup),
+                    _one(graph, issuer, RKAF.proofResolver),
+                    str(_one(graph, lineage, RKAF.modelId)),
+                    _one(graph, proof, RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact),
+                )
+            )
+        if not any(
+            all(left[index] != right[index] for index in range(5))
+            for left, right in combinations(facts, 2)
+        ):
+            violations.add("independence")
+
+        assertion = _one(graph, comparison, RKAF.comparisonExpectedAssertion)
+        stated_relation = _one(graph, assertion, RDF.predicate)
+        verdicts = frozenset(
+            _one(graph, proof, RKAF.adjudicationVerdict) for proof in cited
+        )
+        if _fold_verdicts(verdicts) != stated_relation:
+            violations.add("verdict-lattice")
+    return violations
+
+
+def shape_oracle(graph: Graph) -> set[str]:
+    """Run each emitted rule alone so its Boolean verdict has a stable ID."""
+    all_shapes = Graph().parse(SHAPES_PATH, format="turtle")
+    target_predicates = (
+        SH.targetClass,
+        SH.targetNode,
+        SH.targetSubjectsOf,
+        SH.targetObjectsOf,
+    )
+    violations: set[str] = set()
+    for rule, keep in RULE_SHAPES.items():
+        shapes = Graph()
+        for triple in all_shapes:
+            shapes.add(triple)
+        for predicate in target_predicates:
+            for subject, obj in list(shapes.subject_objects(predicate)):
+                if subject != keep:
+                    shapes.remove((subject, predicate, obj))
+        conforms, _, _ = shacl_validate(
+            graph,
+            shacl_graph=shapes,
+            inference="none",
+            advanced=True,
+            inplace=False,
+            abort_on_first=False,
+            meta_shacl=False,
+        )
+        if not conforms:
+            violations.add(rule)
+    return violations
+
+
+def _fixture_path(case_id: str) -> Path:
+    corpus = json.loads((FIXTURES / "corpus.json").read_bytes())
+    row = next(row for row in corpus["cases"] if row["id"] == case_id)
+    return FIXTURES / row["path"]
+
+
+def _fixture_graph(case_id: str) -> Graph:
+    root = _fixture_path(case_id)
+    if not root.is_dir():
+        raise SystemExit(
+            f"fixture {case_id} is not built; run "
+            "bindings/atlas/3.1/tools/build_fixtures.py first"
+        )
+    manifest = json.loads((root / "atlas-manifest.json").read_bytes())
+    asserted_id = URIRef(
+        next(row["id"] for row in manifest["graphs"] if row["role"] == "asserted")
+    )
+    dataset = Dataset()
+    for pack in manifest["packs"]:
+        payload = (root / pack["path"]).read_bytes()
+        if pack["transport"]["compression"] == "zstd":
+            try:
+                from compression import zstd
+            except ImportError:
+                from backports import zstd
+            payload = zstd.decompress(payload)
+        dataset.parse(data=payload.decode("utf-8"), format="nquads")
+    source = dataset.graph(asserted_id)
+    graph = Graph()
+    for triple in source:
+        graph.add(triple)
+    return graph
+
+
+def _add_proof(graph: Graph, key: str, *, cite: bool = True) -> URIRef:
+    proof = CASE[f"proof-{key}"]
+    issuer = CASE[f"issuer-{key}"]
+    lineage = CASE[f"lineage-{key}"]
+    graph.add((proof, RDF.type, RKAF.ResolverProofRecord))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.proofComparisonContext, CASE.comparison))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.proofIssuer, issuer))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.independenceGroup, CASE[f"group-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.hasAILineage, lineage))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact, CASE[f"response-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.adjudicationVerdict, RKAF.verdictSame))
+    graph.add((issuer, RKAF.proofResolver, CASE[f"provider-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((lineage, RKAF.modelId, Literal(f"model-{key}")))
+    if cite:
+        graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, proof))
+    return proof
+
+
+def _base_graph() -> Graph:
+    graph = Graph()
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome, RKAF.comparisonSatisfied))
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonExpectedAssertion, CASE.assertion))
+    graph.add((CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.exactMatch))
+    _add_proof(graph, "alpha")
+    _add_proof(graph, "beta")
+    return graph
+
+
+def _clone(graph: Graph) -> Graph:
+    result = Graph()
+    for triple in graph:
+        result.add(triple)
+    return result
+
+
+def _replace(graph: Graph, subject: URIRef, predicate: URIRef, value: object) -> None:
+    graph.remove((subject, predicate, None))
+    graph.add((subject, predicate, value))
+
+
+def mutation_cases() -> dict[str, tuple[Graph, set[str]]]:
+    base = _base_graph()
+    cases: dict[str, tuple[Graph, set[str]]] = {"valid-exact": (base, set())}
+
+    single = _clone(base)
+    single.remove((CASE["proof-beta"], None, None))
+    single.remove((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, CASE["proof-beta"]))
+    cases["single-proof"] = (single, {"independence"})
+
+    axis_changes = {
+        "same-actor": (CASE["proof-beta"], RKAF.proofIssuer, CASE["issuer-alpha"]),
+        "same-group": (
+            CASE["proof-beta"],
+            RKAF.independenceGroup,
+            CASE["group-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-response": (
+            CASE["proof-beta"],
+            RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact,
+            CASE["response-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-provider": (
+            CASE["issuer-beta"],
+            RKAF.proofResolver,
+            CASE["provider-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-model": (
+            CASE["lineage-beta"],
+            RKAF.modelId,
+            Literal("model-alpha"),
+        ),
+    }
+    for name, (subject, predicate, value) in axis_changes.items():
+        graph = _clone(base)
+        _replace(graph, subject, predicate, value)
+        cases[name] = (graph, {"independence"})
+
+    discarded = _clone(base)
+    _add_proof(discarded, "gamma", cite=False)
+    cases["discarded-support"] = (discarded, {"complete-support"})
+
+    replay = _clone(base)
+    replay.add((CASE.otherComparison, RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    replay.add((CASE.otherComparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome, RKAF.comparisonRefused))
+    replay.add(
+        (CASE.otherComparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, CASE["proof-alpha"])
+    )
+    cases["proof-replay"] = (replay, {"proof-replay"})
+
+    mixed_exact = _clone(base)
+    _replace(
+        mixed_exact,
+        CASE["proof-beta"],
+        RKAF.adjudicationVerdict,
+        RKAF.verdictNearSame,
+    )
+    cases["exact-with-near"] = (mixed_exact, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    valid_close = _clone(mixed_exact)
+    _replace(valid_close, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.closeMatch)
+    cases["valid-close"] = (valid_close, set())
+
+    close_without_near = _clone(base)
+    _replace(close_without_near, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.closeMatch)
+    cases["close-without-near"] = (close_without_near, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    branches = (
+        ("valid-broad", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetBroader, set()),
+        ("valid-narrow", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower, set()),
+        ("valid-related", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictRelated, set()),
+        ("broad-with-same", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+        ("narrow-with-same", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+        ("related-with-same", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+    )
+    for name, relation, verdict, expected in branches:
+        graph = _clone(base)
+        _replace(graph, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, relation)
+        for key in ("alpha", "beta"):
+            _replace(
+                graph,
+                CASE[f"proof-{key}"],
+                RKAF.adjudicationVerdict,
+                verdict,
+            )
+        cases[name] = (graph, expected)
+
+    unknown = _clone(base)
+    _replace(unknown, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, CASE.unsupportedRelation)
+    cases["unsupported-relation"] = (unknown, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    refused = _clone(mixed_exact)
+    _replace(
+        refused,
+        CASE.comparison,
+        RKAF.comparisonOutcome,
+        RKAF.comparisonRefused,
+    )
+    cases["refused-does-not-fold"] = (refused, set())
+    return cases
+
+
+def _run_case(kind: str, case_id: str, graph: Graph, expected: set[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
+    python = python_oracle(graph)
+    shacl = shape_oracle(graph)
+    if python != shacl or python != expected:
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"{kind}/{case_id}: expected={sorted(expected)}, "
+            f"python={sorted(python)}, shacl={sorted(shacl)}"
+        )
+    return {
+        "expected": sorted(expected),
+        "id": case_id,
+        "kind": kind,
+        "python": sorted(python),
+        "shacl": sorted(shacl),
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output",
+        type=Path,
+        default=ROOT / "research/move2/measurements.json",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    started = time.perf_counter()
+    results = [
+        _run_case("corpus", case_id, _fixture_graph(case_id), expected)
+        for case_id, expected in CORPUS_EXPECTED.items()
+    ]
+    results.extend(
+        _run_case("mutation", case_id, graph, expected)
+        for case_id, (graph, expected) in mutation_cases().items()
+    )
+    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
+    peak = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
+    peak_mib = peak / (1024 * 1024) if sys.platform == "darwin" else peak / 1024
+    summary = {
+        "corpusCases": sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
+        "corpusRuleChecks": 4 * sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
+        "elapsedSeconds": round(elapsed, 3),
+        "engine": "pySHACL 0.31.0",
+        "mutationCases": sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
+        "mutationRuleChecks": 4
+        * sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
+        "peakRssMiB": round(peak_mib, 1),
+        "results": results,
+        "status": "PASS",
+    }
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+    print(
+        f"move-2 oracle PASS: {summary['corpusCases']} corpus + "
+        f"{summary['mutationCases']} mutation cases in {summary['elapsedSeconds']}s; "
+        f"peak RSS {summary['peakRssMiB']} MiB"
+    )
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import ast
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from rdflib import URIRef
+from rdflib.namespace import RDF, SH
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+BINDING = ROOT / "bindings" / "atlas" / "3.1"
+sys.path.insert(0, str(BINDING / "tools"))
+import validate as atlas_validate
+
+EXPECTED_SHAPES = {
+    URIRef("https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#" + local)
+    for local in (
+        "MachineAdjudicationFiveAxisIndependenceShape",
+        "MachineAdjudicationCompleteSupportShape",
+        "MachineAdjudicationVerdictLatticeFoldShape",
+        "MachineAdjudicationProofReplayShape",
+    )
+}
+
+
+def test_binding_loads_the_four_compiler_emitted_shapes_as_local_data() -> None:
+    atlas_validate._check_rulespec_shapes_lock()
+    _, shapes = atlas_validate._parse_binding_graphs()
+    observed = set(shapes.subjects(RDF.type, SH.NodeShape))
+    assert EXPECTED_SHAPES <= observed
+
+
+def test_rulespec_shape_data_and_lock_are_part_of_contract_identity() -> None:
+    baseline = atlas_validate._binding_digests()["contractDigest"]
+    for relative in (
+        Path("shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"),
+        Path("shapes/rulespec-adjudication.lock.json"),
+    ):
+        changed = (BINDING / relative).read_bytes() + b"\n"
+        assert (
+            atlas_validate._binding_digests(content_overrides={relative: changed})[
+                "contractDigest"
+            ]
+            != baseline
+        )
+
+
+def test_copy_and_run_validator_imports_no_rulespec_or_refspec_package() -> None:
+    source = (BINDING / "tools" / "validate.py").read_text()
+    tree = ast.parse(source)
+    imported: set[str] = set()
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
+            imported.update(alias.name.split(".", 1)[0] for alias in node.names)
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
+            imported.add(node.module.split(".", 1)[0])
+    assert "refspec" not in imported

 # recognizes the nested struct by that member rather than by a marker name.

+SHACL_SPARQL_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(
+    r'(?ms)^#(?P<shape>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*Shape)Sparql:\s*"""\n'
+    r'(?P<body>.*?)\n"""\s*$'
+)
+COMPACT_OR_ABSOLUTE_IRI_RE = re.compile(
+    r"^(?:[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:[^\s]+|<[^\s<>]+>)$"
+)
+
+
+def parse_shacl_sparql_annotations(source: str) -> list[SparqlConstraintDef]:
+    """Parse the fail-closed CUE annotation format for graph rules.
+
+    The definition name supplies the stable shape local name. Its multiline
+    string has a generated-scaffolding header, a literal ``---`` separator,
+    then the SPARQL SELECT query::
+
+        #ExampleShapeSparql: <CUE multiline string>
+          targetClass: rkaf:Example
+          message: Explanation shown in a SHACL result.
+          ---
+          PREFIX rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#>
+          SELECT $this WHERE { ... }
+
+    Repeating ``targetClass`` is allowed. Everything else is rejected rather
+    than silently omitted from the emitted constraint.
+    """
+
+    constraints: list[SparqlConstraintDef] = []
+    seen: set[str] = set()
+    for match in SHACL_SPARQL_BLOCK_RE.finditer(source):
+        shape_name = match.group("shape")
+        if shape_name in seen:
+            raise CompileError(f"duplicate SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name}")
+        seen.add(shape_name)
+        header, separator, select = match.group("body").partition("\n---\n")
+        if not separator:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no --- query separator"
+            )
+        targets: list[str] = []
+        message: Optional[str] = None
+        for raw_line in header.splitlines():
+            line = raw_line.strip()
+            if not line:
+                continue
+            key, colon, value = line.partition(":")
+            if not colon or not value.strip():
+                raise CompileError(
+                    f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has malformed header {line!r}"
+                )
+            value = value.strip()
+            if key == "targetClass":
+                if not COMPACT_OR_ABSOLUTE_IRI_RE.fullmatch(value):
+                    raise CompileError(
+                        f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has invalid targetClass {value!r}"
+                    )
+                targets.append(value)
+            elif key == "message":
+                if message is not None:
+                    raise CompileError(
+                        f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} repeats message"
+                    )
+                message = value
+            else:
+                raise CompileError(
+                    f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has unknown header {key!r}"
+                )
+        query = select.strip()
+        if not targets:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no targetClass"
+            )
+        if not message:
+            raise CompileError(f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no message")
+        if not re.search(r"(?i)\bSELECT\s+(?:DISTINCT\s+)?\$this\b", query):
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} must SELECT $this"
+            )
+        if '"""' in query:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} contains a Turtle long-string terminator"
+            )
+        constraints.append(
+            SparqlConstraintDef(
+                shape_name=shape_name,
+                target_classes=targets,
+                message=message,
+                select=query,
+            )
+        )
+    return constraints
+

+# ---- SHACL-SPARQL target (annotated relational rules) --------------------
+
+def target_shacl_sparql(doc: ConstraintDoc) -> str:
+    """Emit only the relational rules explicitly carried by this CUE file."""
+
+    out: list[str] = [
+        "# AUTO-GENERATED by tools/constraints_compile.py "
+        "(target=shacl-sparql).",
+        "# Source: " + (
+            _source_relpath(doc.source_file) or str(doc.source_file or "unknown")
+        ),
+        "# DO NOT EDIT: change the #*ShapeSparql annotation in the CUE source.",
+        "",
+        "@prefix sh:   <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .",
+        "@prefix rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#> .",
+        "",
+    ]
+    for constraint in doc.sparql_constraints:
+        out.append(f"rkaf:{constraint.shape_name} a sh:NodeShape ;")
+        for target_class in constraint.target_classes:
+            out.append(f"  sh:targetClass {target_class} ;")
+        out.extend(
+            (
+                "  sh:sparql [",
+                "    a sh:SPARQLConstraint ;",
+                f"    sh:message {json.dumps(constraint.message)} ;",
+                '    sh:select """',
+                constraint.select,
+                '    """ ;',
+                "  ] .",
+                "",
+            )
+        )
+    return "\n".join(out)

+                "MachineAdjudicationVerdictLatticeFoldShape",
+                "MachineAdjudicationProofReplayShape",

+Four relational adjudication rules are generated by the RuleSpec CUE
+compiler. They reach this copy-and-run binding as plain data in
+`shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl`; the validator still imports no

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Refresh the RuleSpec-owned adjudication shapes vendored into this binding.
+
+The binding validator deliberately imports no RefSpec or RuleSpec package
+code. This development-time generator is the only package-aware side of that
+boundary: it reads compiler output through the installed
+``rulespec_conformance.contract.resources`` accessor, writes plain Turtle
+beside the Atlas shapes, and records exact source and output digests.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from rulespec_conformance.contract import VERSION, resources
+
+BINDING_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+OUTPUT_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"
+LOCK_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.lock.json"
+RESOURCE_NAMES = ("machine-adjudication", "resolver-proof-record")
+
+
+def _digest(payload: bytes) -> str:
+    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _canonical_json(value: object) -> bytes:
+    return (
+        json.dumps(
+            value,
+            ensure_ascii=False,
+            allow_nan=False,
+            sort_keys=True,
+            separators=(",", ":"),
+        ).encode("utf-8")
+        + b"\n"
+    )
+
+
+def render() -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
+    parts = [
+        "# GENERATED by tools/refresh_rulespec_adjudication_shapes.py.",
+        "# Source: rulespec-conformance compiler output; do not edit here.",
+        f"# Rulespec contract version: {VERSION}",
+        "",
+    ]
+    source_rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
+    for name in RESOURCE_NAMES:
+        text = resources.shacl_sparql(name, family="analysis")
+        payload = text.encode("utf-8")
+        source_rows.append(
+            {
+                "accessor": (
+                    "rulespec_conformance.contract.resources."
+                    f"shacl_sparql({name!r}, family='analysis')"
+                ),
+                "byteLength": len(payload),
+                "digest": _digest(payload),
+                "name": name,
+            }
+        )
+        parts.extend((text.rstrip(), ""))
+    output = "\n".join(parts).encode("utf-8")
+    lock = _canonical_json(
+        {
+            "format": "RulespecAdjudicationShapeLock",
+            "formatVersion": "1.0",
+            "output": {
+                "byteLength": len(output),
+                "digest": _digest(output),
+                "path": "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl",
+            },
+            "package": "rulespec-conformance",
+            "packageVersion": VERSION,
+            "resources": source_rows,
+        }
+    )
+    return output, lock
+
+
+def _check(path: Path, expected: bytes) -> bool:
+    if not path.is_file():
+        print(f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} is missing")
+        return False
+    observed = path.read_bytes()
+    if observed != expected:
+        print(
+            f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} differs "
+            f"(expected {_digest(expected)}, found {_digest(observed)})"
+        )
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--check",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="refuse stale generated data instead of refreshing it",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    output, lock = render()
+    if args.check:
+        return 0 if _check(OUTPUT_PATH, output) and _check(LOCK_PATH, lock) else 1
+    OUTPUT_PATH.write_bytes(output)
+    LOCK_PATH.write_bytes(lock)
+    print(
+        "refreshed "
+        f"{OUTPUT_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} ({_digest(output)}) and "
+        f"{LOCK_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)}"
+    )
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+    resources = lock["resources"]
