+        != ["machine-adjudication", "resolver-proof-record"]
+        or any(
+            not isinstance(row, Mapping)
+            or set(row) != {"accessor", "byteLength", "digest", "name"}
+            or not isinstance(row["byteLength"], int)
+            or row["byteLength"] <= 0
+            or not isinstance(row["digest"], str)
+            or not DIGEST_RE.fullmatch(row["digest"])
+            for row in resources
+        )
+    ):

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Differential oracle for compiler-emitted adjudication SHACL-SPARQL.
+
+The Python implementation below is copied and reduced from the four relevant
+parts of ``bindings/atlas/3.1/tools/validate.py``. It deliberately imports
+neither that module nor RuleSpec compiler code: importing the implementation
+being replaced would make agreement circular.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import resource
+import sys
+import time
+from itertools import combinations
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from pyshacl import validate as shacl_validate
+from rdflib import Dataset, Graph, Literal, Namespace, URIRef
+from rdflib.namespace import RDF, SH, SKOS
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+BINDING = ROOT / "bindings/atlas/3.1"
+FIXTURES = BINDING / "fixtures"
+SHAPES_PATH = BINDING / "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"
+
+RKAF = Namespace("https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#")
+CASE = Namespace("urn:ref:move2-oracle:")
+
+RULE_SHAPES = {
+    "independence": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationFiveAxisIndependenceShape,
+    "complete-support": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationCompleteSupportShape,
+    "verdict-lattice": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationVerdictLatticeFoldShape,
+    "proof-replay": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationProofReplayShape,
+}
+
+CORPUS_EXPECTED = {
+    "adjudication-single-proof": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-validator-actor": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-independence-group": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-provider": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-provider-model": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-response-artifact": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-discarded-support": {"complete-support"},
+    "adjudication-relation-not-licensed": {"verdict-lattice"},
+    "adjudication-verdicts-disagree": {"verdict-lattice"},
+    "adjudication-foreign-comparison": {"proof-replay"},
+    "all-resource-profiles": set(),
+    "qualified-three-machine-support": set(),
+    "qualified-lattice-branches": set(),
+    "adjudication-refused-comparison-record": set(),
+}
+
+
+def _one(graph: Graph, subject: URIRef, predicate: URIRef) -> object:
+    values = list(graph.objects(subject, predicate))
+    if len(values) != 1:
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"oracle input requires one {predicate} on {subject}; found {len(values)}"
+        )
+    return values[0]
+
+
+def _fold_verdicts(verdicts: frozenset[object]) -> URIRef | None:
+    """Copied oracle for validate.py::_adjudicated_relation."""
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictSame}:
+        return SKOS.exactMatch
+    if verdicts <= {RKAF.verdictSame, RKAF.verdictNearSame} and (
+        RKAF.verdictNearSame in verdicts
+    ):
+        return SKOS.closeMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetBroader}:
+        return SKOS.broadMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower}:
+        return SKOS.narrowMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictRelated}:
+        return SKOS.relatedMatch
+    return None
+
+
+def python_oracle(graph: Graph) -> set[str]:
+    """Verdicts from the copied old Python behavior for the four rules."""
+    violations: set[str] = set()
+    comparisons = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    proofs = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.ResolverProofRecord))
+
+    for proof in proofs:
+        comparison = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofComparisonContext)
+        if proof not in set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord)):
+            violations.add("complete-support")
+        citing = {
+            subject
+            for subject in graph.subjects(RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, proof)
+            if subject in comparisons
+        }
+        if len(citing) > 1:
+            violations.add("proof-replay")
+
+    for comparison in comparisons:
+        if _one(graph, comparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome) != RKAF.comparisonSatisfied:
+            continue
+        cited = set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord))
+        facts: list[tuple[object, ...]] = []
+        for proof in cited:
+            issuer = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofIssuer)
+            lineage = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.hasAILineage)
+            facts.append(
+                (
+                    issuer,
+                    _one(graph, proof, RKAF.independenceGroup),
+                    _one(graph, issuer, RKAF.proofResolver),
+                    str(_one(graph, lineage, RKAF.modelId)),
+                    _one(graph, proof, RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact),
+                )
+            )
+        if not any(
+            all(left[index] != right[index] for index in range(5))
+            for left, right in combinations(facts, 2)
+        ):
+            violations.add("independence")
+
+        assertion = _one(graph, comparison, RKAF.comparisonExpectedAssertion)
+        stated_relation = _one(graph, assertion, RDF.predicate)
+        verdicts = frozenset(
+            _one(graph, proof, RKAF.adjudicationVerdict) for proof in cited
+        )
+        if _fold_verdicts(verdicts) != stated_relation:
+            violations.add("verdict-lattice")
+    return violations
+
+
+def shape_oracle(graph: Graph) -> set[str]:
+    """Run each emitted rule alone so its Boolean verdict has a stable ID."""
+    all_shapes = Graph().parse(SHAPES_PATH, format="turtle")
+    target_predicates = (
+        SH.targetClass,
+        SH.targetNode,
+        SH.targetSubjectsOf,
+        SH.targetObjectsOf,
+    )
+    violations: set[str] = set()
+    for rule, keep in RULE_SHAPES.items():
+        shapes = Graph()
+        for triple in all_shapes:
+            shapes.add(triple)
+        for predicate in target_predicates:
+            for subject, obj in list(shapes.subject_objects(predicate)):
+                if subject != keep:
+                    shapes.remove((subject, predicate, obj))
+        conforms, _, _ = shacl_validate(
+            graph,
+            shacl_graph=shapes,
+            inference="none",
+            advanced=True,
+            inplace=False,
+            abort_on_first=False,
+            meta_shacl=False,
+        )
+        if not conforms:
+            violations.add(rule)
+    return violations
+
+
+def _fixture_path(case_id: str) -> Path:
+    corpus = json.loads((FIXTURES / "corpus.json").read_bytes())
+    row = next(row for row in corpus["cases"] if row["id"] == case_id)
+    return FIXTURES / row["path"]
+
+
+def _fixture_graph(case_id: str) -> Graph:
+    root = _fixture_path(case_id)
+    if not root.is_dir():
+        raise SystemExit(
+            f"fixture {case_id} is not built; run "
+            "bindings/atlas/3.1/tools/build_fixtures.py first"
+        )
+    manifest = json.loads((root / "atlas-manifest.json").read_bytes())
+    asserted_id = URIRef(
+        next(row["id"] for row in manifest["graphs"] if row["role"] == "asserted")
+    )
+    dataset = Dataset()
+    for pack in manifest["packs"]:
+        payload = (root / pack["path"]).read_bytes()
+        if pack["transport"]["compression"] == "zstd":
+            try:
+                from compression import zstd
+            except ImportError:
+                from backports import zstd
+            payload = zstd.decompress(payload)
+        dataset.parse(data=payload.decode("utf-8"), format="nquads")
+    source = dataset.graph(asserted_id)
+    graph = Graph()
+    for triple in source:
+        graph.add(triple)
+    return graph
+
+
+def _add_proof(graph: Graph, key: str, *, cite: bool = True) -> URIRef:
+    proof = CASE[f"proof-{key}"]
+    issuer = CASE[f"issuer-{key}"]
+    lineage = CASE[f"lineage-{key}"]
+    graph.add((proof, RDF.type, RKAF.ResolverProofRecord))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.proofComparisonContext, CASE.comparison))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.proofIssuer, issuer))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.independenceGroup, CASE[f"group-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.hasAILineage, lineage))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact, CASE[f"response-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.adjudicationVerdict, RKAF.verdictSame))
+    graph.add((issuer, RKAF.proofResolver, CASE[f"provider-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((lineage, RKAF.modelId, Literal(f"model-{key}")))
+    if cite:
+        graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, proof))
+    return proof
+
+
+def _base_graph() -> Graph:
+    graph = Graph()
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome, RKAF.comparisonSatisfied))
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonExpectedAssertion, CASE.assertion))
+    graph.add((CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.exactMatch))
+    _add_proof(graph, "alpha")
+    _add_proof(graph, "beta")
+    return graph
+
+
+def _clone(graph: Graph) -> Graph:
+    result = Graph()
+    for triple in graph:
+        result.add(triple)
+    return result
+
+
+def _replace(graph: Graph, subject: URIRef, predicate: URIRef, value: object) -> None:
+    graph.remove((subject, predicate, None))
+    graph.add((subject, predicate, value))
+
+
+def mutation_cases() -> dict[str, tuple[Graph, set[str]]]:
+    base = _base_graph()
+    cases: dict[str, tuple[Graph, set[str]]] = {"valid-exact": (base, set())}
+
+    single = _clone(base)
+    single.remove((CASE["proof-beta"], None, None))
+    single.remove((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, CASE["proof-beta"]))
+    cases["single-proof"] = (single, {"independence"})
+
+    axis_changes = {
+        "same-actor": (CASE["proof-beta"], RKAF.proofIssuer, CASE["issuer-alpha"]),
+        "same-group": (
+            CASE["proof-beta"],
+            RKAF.independenceGroup,
+            CASE["group-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-response": (
+            CASE["proof-beta"],
+            RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact,
+            CASE["response-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-provider": (
+            CASE["issuer-beta"],
+            RKAF.proofResolver,
+            CASE["provider-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-model": (
+            CASE["lineage-beta"],
+            RKAF.modelId,
+            Literal("model-alpha"),
+        ),
+    }
+    for name, (subject, predicate, value) in axis_changes.items():
+        graph = _clone(base)
+        _replace(graph, subject, predicate, value)
+        cases[name] = (graph, {"independence"})
+
+    discarded = _clone(base)
+    _add_proof(discarded, "gamma", cite=False)
+    cases["discarded-support"] = (discarded, {"complete-support"})
+
+    replay = _clone(base)
+    replay.add((CASE.otherComparison, RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    replay.add((CASE.otherComparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome, RKAF.comparisonRefused))
+    replay.add(
+        (CASE.otherComparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, CASE["proof-alpha"])
+    )
+    cases["proof-replay"] = (replay, {"proof-replay"})
+
+    mixed_exact = _clone(base)
+    _replace(
+        mixed_exact,
+        CASE["proof-beta"],
+        RKAF.adjudicationVerdict,
+        RKAF.verdictNearSame,
+    )
+    cases["exact-with-near"] = (mixed_exact, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    valid_close = _clone(mixed_exact)
+    _replace(valid_close, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.closeMatch)
+    cases["valid-close"] = (valid_close, set())
+
+    close_without_near = _clone(base)
+    _replace(close_without_near, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.closeMatch)
+    cases["close-without-near"] = (close_without_near, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    branches = (
+        ("valid-broad", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetBroader, set()),
+        ("valid-narrow", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower, set()),
+        ("valid-related", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictRelated, set()),
+        ("broad-with-same", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+        ("narrow-with-same", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+        ("related-with-same", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+    )
+    for name, relation, verdict, expected in branches:
+        graph = _clone(base)
+        _replace(graph, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, relation)
+        for key in ("alpha", "beta"):
+            _replace(
+                graph,
+                CASE[f"proof-{key}"],
+                RKAF.adjudicationVerdict,
+                verdict,
+            )
+        cases[name] = (graph, expected)
+
+    unknown = _clone(base)
+    _replace(unknown, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, CASE.unsupportedRelation)
+    cases["unsupported-relation"] = (unknown, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    refused = _clone(mixed_exact)
+    _replace(
+        refused,
+        CASE.comparison,
+        RKAF.comparisonOutcome,
+        RKAF.comparisonRefused,
+    )
+    cases["refused-does-not-fold"] = (refused, set())
+    return cases
+
+
+def _run_case(kind: str, case_id: str, graph: Graph, expected: set[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
+    python = python_oracle(graph)
+    shacl = shape_oracle(graph)
+    if python != shacl or python != expected:
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"{kind}/{case_id}: expected={sorted(expected)}, "
+            f"python={sorted(python)}, shacl={sorted(shacl)}"
+        )
+    return {
+        "expected": sorted(expected),
+        "id": case_id,
+        "kind": kind,
+        "python": sorted(python),
+        "shacl": sorted(shacl),
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output",
+        type=Path,
+        default=ROOT / "research/move2/measurements.json",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    started = time.perf_counter()
+    results = [
+        _run_case("corpus", case_id, _fixture_graph(case_id), expected)
+        for case_id, expected in CORPUS_EXPECTED.items()
+    ]
+    results.extend(
+        _run_case("mutation", case_id, graph, expected)
+        for case_id, (graph, expected) in mutation_cases().items()
+    )
+    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
+    peak = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
+    peak_mib = peak / (1024 * 1024) if sys.platform == "darwin" else peak / 1024
+    summary = {
+        "corpusCases": sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
+        "corpusRuleChecks": 4 * sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
+        "elapsedSeconds": round(elapsed, 3),
+        "engine": "pySHACL 0.31.0",
+        "mutationCases": sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
+        "mutationRuleChecks": 4
+        * sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
+        "peakRssMiB": round(peak_mib, 1),
+        "results": results,
+        "status": "PASS",
+    }
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+    print(
+        f"move-2 oracle PASS: {summary['corpusCases']} corpus + "
+        f"{summary['mutationCases']} mutation cases in {summary['elapsedSeconds']}s; "
+        f"peak RSS {summary['peakRssMiB']} MiB"
+    )
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import ast
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from rdflib import URIRef
+from rdflib.namespace import RDF, SH
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+BINDING = ROOT / "bindings" / "atlas" / "3.1"
+sys.path.insert(0, str(BINDING / "tools"))
+import validate as atlas_validate
+
+EXPECTED_SHAPES = {
+    URIRef("https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#" + local)
+    for local in (
+        "MachineAdjudicationFiveAxisIndependenceShape",
+        "MachineAdjudicationCompleteSupportShape",
+        "MachineAdjudicationVerdictLatticeFoldShape",
+        "MachineAdjudicationProofReplayShape",
+    )
+}
+
+
+def test_binding_loads_the_four_compiler_emitted_shapes_as_local_data() -> None:
+    atlas_validate._check_rulespec_shapes_lock()
+    _, shapes = atlas_validate._parse_binding_graphs()
+    observed = set(shapes.subjects(RDF.type, SH.NodeShape))
+    assert EXPECTED_SHAPES <= observed
+
+
+def test_rulespec_shape_data_and_lock_are_part_of_contract_identity() -> None:
+    baseline = atlas_validate._binding_digests()["contractDigest"]
+    for relative in (
+        Path("shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"),
+        Path("shapes/rulespec-adjudication.lock.json"),
+    ):
+        changed = (BINDING / relative).read_bytes() + b"\n"
+        assert (
+            atlas_validate._binding_digests(content_overrides={relative: changed})[
+                "contractDigest"
+            ]
+            != baseline
+        )
+
+
+def test_copy_and_run_validator_imports_no_rulespec_or_refspec_package() -> None:
+    source = (BINDING / "tools" / "validate.py").read_text()
+    tree = ast.parse(source)
+    imported: set[str] = set()
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
+            imported.update(alias.name.split(".", 1)[0] for alias in node.names)
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
+            imported.add(node.module.split(".", 1)[0])
+    assert "refspec" not in imported
+    assert "rulespec_conformance" not in imported

1340:### REF-029: Contract identity and proof identity are two different digests
   476	## The rulespec boundary, collapsed (v3.2)
   477	
   478	Constraint update: **rulespec is ours.** Any upstream change is in scope if
   479	it reduces code, improves DX/dev speed, and adds no future architectural
   480	debt. Three moves, in order of (payoff ÷ risk):
   481	
   482	1. **Ship rulespec as a versioned package, not a sibling checkout.** One
   483	   `rulespec` (or `rkaf`) package carrying: compiled JSON Schemas, compiled
   484	   SHACL, JSON-LD context, generated Python types, and the lattices/enums
   485	   **as importable data**. RefSpec takes it via `uv add` like any
   486	   dependency. Deletes in RefSpec: checkout discovery
   487	   (`REFSPEC_RULESPEC_CHECKOUT`), `validate_rulespec_gate.py` (150),
   488	   `test_rulespec_vocabulary_currency.py` (297 — an unknown rkaf term
   489	   becomes an ImportError at build: fix-by-construction replaces text
   490	   scanning), `test_usage_eligibility_lattice_currency.py` (199 — the three
   491	   lattice copies become `from rkaf import USAGE_ELIGIBILITY`), the
   492	   dependency-manifest self-certification ceremony, and the subprocess
   493	   pinning of Rust CLIs on RefSpec's path (Rust validators remain for
   494	   rulespec's own CI and any external consumer). Also ends the
   495	   worktree/uv-cache cross-repo build pain. Contract bumps become lockfile
   496	   bumps. **Working precedent as of 2026-08-11:** rulespec-conformance
   497	   already ships as a wheel verified from an installed package with no
   498	   checkout (`make test-package`), and spicy-regs PLAN.md §6 schedules the
   499	   editable-install deletion on its side — this move extends an existing
   500	   pattern, not a new bet.
   501	2. **One implementation per rule: the CUE compiler emits the check;
   502	   consumers execute, never re-implement.** The adjudication protocol's
   503	   constraints (five-axis independence, warrant closure, verdict lattice)
   504	   compile from CUE into the published SHACL (`sh:sparql` where shapes
   505	   can't express them) plus, where SPARQL genuinely can't say it, a small
   506	   Python gate module *inside the rulespec package*, tested once upstream.
   507	   RefSpec's ~900 protocol lines shrink to invocations. The 4-vs-5-axis
   508	   defect class (shipped SHACL disagreeing with prose and runtime) dies
   509	   structurally: there is nothing downstream left to disagree.
   510	3. **Decide the monorepo deliberately.** The 2026-08-04 deferral of
   511	   shared-foundation unification predates this measurement of what the
   512	   boundary costs. If no third party consumes rulespec releases today, a uv
   513	   workspace monorepo makes contract + consumer + fixtures one atomic
   514	   commit and deletes inter-repo versioning permanently; packages still
   515	   publish separately from a workspace, so the portability story survives.
   516	   If the answer is no, move 1 alone captures most of the value.
   517	
   518	Guardrails (the debt this section must not create): rulespec stays generic —
   519	no Atlas-specific terms or checks migrate upstream (boundary inversion is
   520	the one way this collapse rots); rkaf remains the single ontology; RefSpec
   521	never re-grows a local copy of anything the package exports.
   522	
   523	## What the 2h instrumented run changes (v3.3)
   524	
   525	1. **Red builds must be fast — the failure path is 20× the success path,
   526	   which is backwards for development.** The 94 SHACL minutes were the
   527	   *fallback*: the batched prechecks detected a miss in seconds-to-minutes,
   528	   then the full normative engine ran solely to phrase the report. You
   529	   iterate on red builds; today a red build costs ~2h to say "evidence
   530	   bindings are wrong." Change: dev-mode validation reports from the fast
   531	   path's own miss detection (it knows which lifted constraint failed on
   532	   which nodes) or re-validates only the failing focus nodes
   533	   (`abort_on_first` / targeted shapes); the full normative report becomes
   534	   release/audit-mode only.
   535	2. **Sample-first smoke tier.** All 2,003 violations were the same defect;
   536	   one evidence binding validated at fixture scale (~50ms) would have
   537	   caught it. Dev builds shape-check a bounded sample per pack (seconds);
   538	   the full pass runs only in the release workflow. Test-pyramid economics
   539	   applied to data, not just code.
   540	3. **Release-runner spec is now measurable:** ≥32 GB RAM (18.3 GB RSS at
   541	   parse alone), ~1h wall budget, single beefy core beats many small ones
   542	   (the pipeline is serial and memory-bound; naive multiprocess parsing
   543	   multiplies the 18 GB, it does not divide the wall).
   544	4. **The phase table is COMPLETE (2026-08-12, conforming 08-12 build —
   545	   the first full multi-scheme distribution to pass HEAD's binding
   546	   independently; 32,011,869 quads, 4,539.8s ≈ 75.7 min, 23.6 GB peak).**
   547	   Split: SHACL fast-path green 1,957s (43.1%); parse 1,373s (30.2%);
   548	   graph-roles 570s (12.6%); compact sample 209s + node digests 131s +
   549	   evidence/assertions 145s + accounting 87s ≈ 12%; SKOS integrity 5.2s;
   550	   adjudication 9.5s; reasoning isolation/derived/projection ~0 (empty
   551	   layers). Verdict: the integrity phases the reset's diagnosis blamed are
   552	   ~7.5% of acceptance — the wall is the SHACL engine + rdflib parse,
   553	   which is where kill-5's engine contingency already points and which
   554	   runs once per release. The wire cuts stand on no-consumer grounds, as
   555	   stated. The hand-written SKOS bitset machinery is measured at 0.1% —
   556	   structure that earned its keep.
   557	
   558	   **Inside-the-phases trace (fable, live-sampled + staging-profiled,
   559	   2026-08-12, 3.1 run ≈62 min):** ~67% of the SHACL phase (~21 min of the
   560	   hour) is the warrant `sh:xone` evaluated by engine trial — ~3.5M branch
   561	   validations, five of six failing by design, each minting a discarded
   562	   pretty-printed report. The guarantee is a six-entry frozenset; the lift
   563	   pattern exists in-code (`_can_lift_relation_ring_context`), A/B measured
   564	   151× at staging. Parse = 60% rdflib substrate + 28% canonicality proof
   565	   (KEEP — it carries the consumer's identity digests) + 12% bookkeeping.
   566	   graph-roles' 500s is CPU-bound store iteration; half folds into the
   567	   parse observer. Sanctioned optimizations (kill-5 pattern, no new
   568	   decision): xone lift (−~21 min), gc.freeze after parse (−1-2 min),
   569	   graph-roles sweep fold (−~4 min) → **62 → ~37 min**; the residual floor
   570	   is rdflib, and only the pre-approved kill-5 subprocess engine goes
   571	   below it — not needed at once-per-release frequency.
   572	   **IMPLEMENTED and measured at staging (2026-08-12): total 91→53s
   573	   (−42%), SHACL −68% (xone lifted by parsing the branch table off the
   574	   wire — semantics never restated; a drifted shape refuses the lift
   575	   loudly and falls back to the engine; the pinned signature must move
   576	   WITH any future warrant-model amendment), graph-roles −79% (parse
   577	   observer, same codes/messages, failure order now deterministic),
   578	   peak RSS −37%. Corpus byte-unchanged; all 47 shacl.data cases agree
   579	   across fail-fast/audit/published components. Projected full scale:
   580	   ~32–36 min. Engine-door spikes (oxigraph substrate, Jena SHACL) are
   581	   measuring the rungs below in parallel worktrees.**

   583	## Target architecture: minimum required, by industry standard
   584	
   585	| Actual feature | Standard carrier | Bespoke remainder |
   586	|---|---|---|
   587	| Vocabulary releases | SKOS/SKOS-XL, versioned distributions | publisher ETL adapters |
   588	| Mapping statements | SKOS `skos:*Match` triples (projection) | — |
   589	| Mapping evidence + adjudication | rkaf (upstream contract — no standard substitute) | ~900 lines at acceptance |
   590	| Mapping interchange | SSSOM + SEMAPV — **deferred** until a consumer names itself | derived TSV view, then |
   591	| Semantic conformance | SHACL (pySHACL or measured fallback) | shapes + one gate module |
   592	| Canonical bytes | RDFC-1.0 / sorted skolemized N-Quads at write | none — serializer property |
   593	| Integrity & trust | detached signature per Seal design | ~100-line `verify_seal` |
   594	| Independent assurance | reproducible rebuild (SLSA/reproducible-builds practice) | scheduled job |
   595	| Serving | Parquet + DuckDB, fed directly from the builder | view builder |
   596	| Provenance | W3C PROV (via rkaf) | none |
   597	| Transcription fidelity | no standard exists | the auditor — the differentiator |
   598	
   599	**SSSOM, re-scoped (v3.1): deferred derived view, not carrier.** SSSOM
   600	covers the mapping statement + curation provenance (justification, author,
   601	confidence, tool, versions). It does NOT carry what rulespec provides:
   602	evidence bindings pinning sealed source-record digests, the adjudication
   603	proof chain, lifecycle/supersession temporal records, or the contract
   604	relationship itself (rkaf = CUE-authored constraints with upstream
   605	validators; SSSOM = column conventions). A carrier swap would need an
   606	upstream RuleSpec decision and an evidence-model redesign to migrate 2,003
   607	assertions whose ~900 lines of checks run at acceptance, where cost is
   608	already irrelevant. Resolution: **rkaf remains the mapping carrier** (one
   609	ontology, upstream-validated, cheap at acceptance frequency); the plan
   610	becomes fully RefSpec-local with no cross-repo dependency. **Keep the
   611	`skos:*Match` projection triples in the RDF** — ~2k triples, the
   612	W3C-standard publication form; deferring them saves nothing.
   613	
   614	**Prior art — SSSOM was tried and retired, and the difference matters.**
   615	`3e975876` (2026-08-03) built a real SSSOM TSV exporter (deterministic,
   616	edition-scoped prefixes because Bioregistry's `elsst` record expands to
   617	edition 3 and would rewrite R6 IRIs; per-row `urn:` mapping_source; sssom-py
   618	round-trip oracle). `5ed56db5` deleted it with the crosswalk runtime;
   619	`546c4940` (2026-08-10) deleted the last README promise because the exporter
   620	had no production writer and no consumer — SSSOM as a *bolt-on second view*
   621	died, correctly. This plan proposes SSSOM as the *primary carrier replacing*
   622	the bespoke reification: the build is the writer, sssom-py the validator,
   623	deletion economics the justification — which satisfies `546c4940`'s own
   624	revival clause ("a real producer and consumer appear"). v3.1 resolution:
   625	that clause is the standing trigger. SSSOM returns only as a build-derived
   626	TSV view when a real external consumer names itself (curation workflow, OAK
   627	tooling, a mapping partner); the build is then the writer, sssom-py the
   628	gate, and the exporter's lessons (edition-scoped prefixes, `urn:`
   629	mapping_source, oracle round-trip) are recovered from `5ed56db5^` rather
   630	than re-learned. Building it before the trigger fires repeats the mistake
   631	retired on 08-10. The orphaned `sssom` dev dependency is removed until then.
   632	
   633	Entitled bespoke code: (1) publisher adapters, (2) shapes + one gate module,
   634	(3) the fidelity auditor, (4) the seal, (5) the reproducible-rebuild job.
   635	
   636	Check regime: **build** = SHACL + sssom-py + manifest JSON Schema + semantic
   637	gates + canonicality/reproducibility pass + sign-with-receipt. **read** =
   638	verify seal. **audit** (scheduled) = fidelity auditor + reproducible rebuild
   639	+ full validator on a shipped artifact. **dev loop** = lint + parquet
   640	preflight, with `make test` under a 60s budget (warn >60s; hard FAIL at
   641	240s as a runaway guard — the 120s line re-arms once the suite is next
   642	measured under 60s; see the budget re-spec open item).

 # recognizes the nested struct by that member rather than by a marker name.

+SHACL_SPARQL_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(
+    r'(?ms)^#(?P<shape>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*Shape)Sparql:\s*"""\n'
+    r'(?P<body>.*?)\n"""\s*$'
+)
+COMPACT_OR_ABSOLUTE_IRI_RE = re.compile(
+    r"^(?:[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:[^\s]+|<[^\s<>]+>)$"
+)
+
+
+def parse_shacl_sparql_annotations(source: str) -> list[SparqlConstraintDef]:
+    """Parse the fail-closed CUE annotation format for graph rules.
+
+    The definition name supplies the stable shape local name. Its multiline
+    string has a generated-scaffolding header, a literal ``---`` separator,
+    then the SPARQL SELECT query::
+
+        #ExampleShapeSparql: <CUE multiline string>
+          targetClass: rkaf:Example
+          message: Explanation shown in a SHACL result.
+          ---
+          PREFIX rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#>
+          SELECT $this WHERE { ... }
+
+    Repeating ``targetClass`` is allowed. Everything else is rejected rather
+    than silently omitted from the emitted constraint.
+    """
+
+    constraints: list[SparqlConstraintDef] = []
+    seen: set[str] = set()
+    for match in SHACL_SPARQL_BLOCK_RE.finditer(source):
+        shape_name = match.group("shape")
+        if shape_name in seen:
+            raise CompileError(f"duplicate SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name}")
+        seen.add(shape_name)
+        header, separator, select = match.group("body").partition("\n---\n")
+        if not separator:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no --- query separator"
+            )
+        targets: list[str] = []
+        message: Optional[str] = None
+        for raw_line in header.splitlines():
+            line = raw_line.strip()
+            if not line:
+                continue
+            key, colon, value = line.partition(":")
+            if not colon or not value.strip():
+                raise CompileError(
+                    f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has malformed header {line!r}"
+                )
+            value = value.strip()
+            if key == "targetClass":
+                if not COMPACT_OR_ABSOLUTE_IRI_RE.fullmatch(value):
+                    raise CompileError(
+                        f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has invalid targetClass {value!r}"
+                    )
+                targets.append(value)
+            elif key == "message":
+                if message is not None:
+                    raise CompileError(
+                        f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} repeats message"
+                    )
+                message = value
+            else:
+                raise CompileError(
+                    f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has unknown header {key!r}"
+                )
+        query = select.strip()
+        if not targets:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no targetClass"
+            )
+        if not message:
+            raise CompileError(f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no message")
+        if not re.search(r"(?i)\bSELECT\s+(?:DISTINCT\s+)?\$this\b", query):
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} must SELECT $this"
+            )
+        if '"""' in query:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} contains a Turtle long-string terminator"
+            )
+        constraints.append(
+            SparqlConstraintDef(
+                shape_name=shape_name,
+                target_classes=targets,
+                message=message,
+                select=query,
+            )
+        )
+    return constraints
+

+# ---- SHACL-SPARQL target (annotated relational rules) --------------------
+
+def target_shacl_sparql(doc: ConstraintDoc) -> str:
+    """Emit only the relational rules explicitly carried by this CUE file."""
+
+    out: list[str] = [
+        "# AUTO-GENERATED by tools/constraints_compile.py "
+        "(target=shacl-sparql).",
+        "# Source: " + (
+            _source_relpath(doc.source_file) or str(doc.source_file or "unknown")
+        ),
+        "# DO NOT EDIT: change the #*ShapeSparql annotation in the CUE source.",
+        "",
+        "@prefix sh:   <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .",
+        "@prefix rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#> .",
+        "",
+    ]
+    for constraint in doc.sparql_constraints:
+        out.append(f"rkaf:{constraint.shape_name} a sh:NodeShape ;")
+        for target_class in constraint.target_classes:
+            out.append(f"  sh:targetClass {target_class} ;")
+        out.extend(
+            (
+                "  sh:sparql [",
+                "    a sh:SPARQLConstraint ;",
+                f"    sh:message {json.dumps(constraint.message)} ;",
+                '    sh:select """',
+                constraint.select,
+                '    """ ;',
+                "  ] .",
+                "",
+            )
+        )
+    return "\n".join(out)
+

+        graph = Graph()

+                "MachineAdjudicationProofReplayShape",

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Refresh the RuleSpec-owned adjudication shapes vendored into this binding.
+
+The binding validator deliberately imports no RefSpec or RuleSpec package
+code. This development-time generator is the only package-aware side of that
+boundary: it reads compiler output through the installed
+``rulespec_conformance.contract.resources`` accessor, writes plain Turtle
+beside the Atlas shapes, and records exact source and output digests.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from rulespec_conformance.contract import VERSION, resources
+
+BINDING_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+OUTPUT_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"
+LOCK_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.lock.json"
+RESOURCE_NAMES = ("machine-adjudication", "resolver-proof-record")
+
+
+def _digest(payload: bytes) -> str:
+    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _canonical_json(value: object) -> bytes:
+    return (
+        json.dumps(
+            value,
+            ensure_ascii=False,
+            allow_nan=False,
+            sort_keys=True,
+            separators=(",", ":"),
+        ).encode("utf-8")
+        + b"\n"
+    )
+
+
+def render() -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
+    parts = [
+        "# GENERATED by tools/refresh_rulespec_adjudication_shapes.py.",
+        "# Source: rulespec-conformance compiler output; do not edit here.",
+        f"# Rulespec contract version: {VERSION}",
+        "",
+    ]
+    source_rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
+    for name in RESOURCE_NAMES:
+        text = resources.shacl_sparql(name, family="analysis")
+        payload = text.encode("utf-8")
+        source_rows.append(
+            {
+                "accessor": (
+                    "rulespec_conformance.contract.resources."
+                    f"shacl_sparql({name!r}, family='analysis')"
+                ),
+                "byteLength": len(payload),
+                "digest": _digest(payload),
+                "name": name,
+            }
+        )
+        parts.extend((text.rstrip(), ""))
+    output = "\n".join(parts).encode("utf-8")
+    lock = _canonical_json(
+        {
+            "format": "RulespecAdjudicationShapeLock",
+            "formatVersion": "1.0",
+            "output": {
+                "byteLength": len(output),
+                "digest": _digest(output),
+                "path": "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl",
+            },
+            "package": "rulespec-conformance",
+            "packageVersion": VERSION,
+            "resources": source_rows,
+        }
+    )
+    return output, lock
+
+
+def _check(path: Path, expected: bytes) -> bool:
+    if not path.is_file():
+        print(f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} is missing")
+        return False
+    observed = path.read_bytes()
+    if observed != expected:
+        print(
+            f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} differs "
+            f"(expected {_digest(expected)}, found {_digest(observed)})"
+        )
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--check",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="refuse stale generated data instead of refreshing it",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    output, lock = render()
+    if args.check:
+        return 0 if _check(OUTPUT_PATH, output) and _check(LOCK_PATH, lock) else 1
+    OUTPUT_PATH.write_bytes(output)
+    LOCK_PATH.write_bytes(lock)
+    print(
+        "refreshed "
+        f"{OUTPUT_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} ({_digest(output)}) and "
+        f"{LOCK_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)}"
+    )
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Differential oracle for compiler-emitted adjudication SHACL-SPARQL.
+
+The Python implementation below is copied and reduced from the four relevant
+parts of ``bindings/atlas/3.1/tools/validate.py``. It deliberately imports
+neither that module nor RuleSpec compiler code: importing the implementation
+being replaced would make agreement circular.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import resource
+import sys
+import time
+from itertools import combinations
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from pyshacl import validate as shacl_validate
+from rdflib import Dataset, Graph, Literal, Namespace, URIRef
+from rdflib.namespace import RDF, SH, SKOS
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+BINDING = ROOT / "bindings/atlas/3.1"
+FIXTURES = BINDING / "fixtures"
+SHAPES_PATH = BINDING / "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"
+
+RKAF = Namespace("https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#")
+CASE = Namespace("urn:ref:move2-oracle:")
+
+RULE_SHAPES = {
+    "independence": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationFiveAxisIndependenceShape,
+    "complete-support": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationCompleteSupportShape,
+    "verdict-lattice": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationVerdictLatticeFoldShape,
+    "proof-replay": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationProofReplayShape,
+}
+
+CORPUS_EXPECTED = {
+    "adjudication-single-proof": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-validator-actor": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-independence-group": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-provider": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-provider-model": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-response-artifact": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-discarded-support": {"complete-support"},
+    "adjudication-relation-not-licensed": {"verdict-lattice"},
+    "adjudication-verdicts-disagree": {"verdict-lattice"},
+    "adjudication-foreign-comparison": {"proof-replay"},
+    "all-resource-profiles": set(),
+    "qualified-three-machine-support": set(),
+    "qualified-lattice-branches": set(),
+    "adjudication-refused-comparison-record": set(),
+}
+
+
+def _one(graph: Graph, subject: URIRef, predicate: URIRef) -> object:
+    values = list(graph.objects(subject, predicate))
+    if len(values) != 1:
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"oracle input requires one {predicate} on {subject}; found {len(values)}"
+        )
+    return values[0]
+
+
+def _fold_verdicts(verdicts: frozenset[object]) -> URIRef | None:
+    """Copied oracle for validate.py::_adjudicated_relation."""
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictSame}:
+        return SKOS.exactMatch
+    if verdicts <= {RKAF.verdictSame, RKAF.verdictNearSame} and (
+        RKAF.verdictNearSame in verdicts
+    ):
+        return SKOS.closeMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetBroader}:
+        return SKOS.broadMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower}:
+        return SKOS.narrowMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictRelated}:
+        return SKOS.relatedMatch
+    return None
+
+
+def python_oracle(graph: Graph) -> set[str]:
+    """Verdicts from the copied old Python behavior for the four rules."""
+    violations: set[str] = set()
+    comparisons = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    proofs = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.ResolverProofRecord))
+
+    for proof in proofs:
+        comparison = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofComparisonContext)
+        if proof not in set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord)):
+            violations.add("complete-support")
+        citing = {
+            subject
+            for subject in graph.subjects(RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, proof)
+            if subject in comparisons
+        }
+        if len(citing) > 1:
+            violations.add("proof-replay")
+
+    for comparison in comparisons:
+        if _one(graph, comparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome) != RKAF.comparisonSatisfied:
+            continue
+        cited = set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord))
+        facts: list[tuple[object, ...]] = []
+        for proof in cited:
+            issuer = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofIssuer)
+            lineage = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.hasAILineage)
+            facts.append(
+                (
+                    issuer,
+                    _one(graph, proof, RKAF.independenceGroup),
+                    _one(graph, issuer, RKAF.proofResolver),
+                    str(_one(graph, lineage, RKAF.modelId)),
+                    _one(graph, proof, RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact),
+                )
+            )
+        if not any(
+            all(left[index] != right[index] for index in range(5))
+            for left, right in combinations(facts, 2)
+        ):
+            violations.add("independence")
+
+        assertion = _one(graph, comparison, RKAF.comparisonExpectedAssertion)
+        stated_relation = _one(graph, assertion, RDF.predicate)
+        verdicts = frozenset(
+            _one(graph, proof, RKAF.adjudicationVerdict) for proof in cited
+        )
+        if _fold_verdicts(verdicts) != stated_relation:
+            violations.add("verdict-lattice")
+    return violations
+
+
+def shape_oracle(graph: Graph) -> set[str]:
+    """Run each emitted rule alone so its Boolean verdict has a stable ID."""
+    all_shapes = Graph().parse(SHAPES_PATH, format="turtle")
+    target_predicates = (
+        SH.targetClass,
+        SH.targetNode,
+        SH.targetSubjectsOf,
+        SH.targetObjectsOf,
+    )
+    violations: set[str] = set()
+    for rule, keep in RULE_SHAPES.items():
+        shapes = Graph()
+        for triple in all_shapes:
+            shapes.add(triple)
+        for predicate in target_predicates:
+            for subject, obj in list(shapes.subject_objects(predicate)):
+                if subject != keep:
+                    shapes.remove((subject, predicate, obj))
+        conforms, _, _ = shacl_validate(
+            graph,
+            shacl_graph=shapes,
+            inference="none",
+            advanced=True,
+            inplace=False,
+            abort_on_first=False,
+            meta_shacl=False,
+        )
+        if not conforms:
+            violations.add(rule)
+    return violations
+
+
+def _fixture_path(case_id: str) -> Path:
+    corpus = json.loads((FIXTURES / "corpus.json").read_bytes())
+    row = next(row for row in corpus["cases"] if row["id"] == case_id)
+    return FIXTURES / row["path"]
+
+
+def _fixture_graph(case_id: str) -> Graph:
+    root = _fixture_path(case_id)
+    if not root.is_dir():
+        raise SystemExit(
+            f"fixture {case_id} is not built; run "
+            "bindings/atlas/3.1/tools/build_fixtures.py first"
+        )
+    manifest = json.loads((root / "atlas-manifest.json").read_bytes())
+    asserted_id = URIRef(
+        next(row["id"] for row in manifest["graphs"] if row["role"] == "asserted")
+    )
+    dataset = Dataset()
+    for pack in manifest["packs"]:
+        payload = (root / pack["path"]).read_bytes()
+        if pack["transport"]["compression"] == "zstd":
+            try:
+                from compression import zstd
+            except ImportError:
+                from backports import zstd
+            payload = zstd.decompress(payload)
+        dataset.parse(data=payload.decode("utf-8"), format="nquads")
+    source = dataset.graph(asserted_id)
+    graph = Graph()
+    for triple in source:
+        graph.add(triple)
+    return graph
+
+
+def _add_proof(graph: Graph, key: str, *, cite: bool = True) -> URIRef:
+    proof = CASE[f"proof-{key}"]
+    issuer = CASE[f"issuer-{key}"]
+    lineage = CASE[f"lineage-{key}"]
+    graph.add((proof, RDF.type, RKAF.ResolverProofRecord))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.proofComparisonContext, CASE.comparison))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.proofIssuer, issuer))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.independenceGroup, CASE[f"group-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.hasAILineage, lineage))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact, CASE[f"response-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.adjudicationVerdict, RKAF.verdictSame))
+    graph.add((issuer, RKAF.proofResolver, CASE[f"provider-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((lineage, RKAF.modelId, Literal(f"model-{key}")))
+    if cite:
+        graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, proof))
+    return proof
+
+
+def _base_graph() -> Graph:
+    graph = Graph()
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome, RKAF.comparisonSatisfied))
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonExpectedAssertion, CASE.assertion))
+    graph.add((CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.exactMatch))
+    _add_proof(graph, "alpha")
+    _add_proof(graph, "beta")
+    return graph
+
+
+def _clone(graph: Graph) -> Graph:
+    result = Graph()
+    for triple in graph:
+        result.add(triple)
+    return result
+
+
+def _replace(graph: Graph, subject: URIRef, predicate: URIRef, value: object) -> None:
+    graph.remove((subject, predicate, None))
+    graph.add((subject, predicate, value))
+
+
+def mutation_cases() -> dict[str, tuple[Graph, set[str]]]:
+    base = _base_graph()
+    cases: dict[str, tuple[Graph, set[str]]] = {"valid-exact": (base, set())}
+
+    single = _clone(base)
+    single.remove((CASE["proof-beta"], None, None))
+    single.remove((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, CASE["proof-beta"]))
+    cases["single-proof"] = (single, {"independence"})
+
+    axis_changes = {
+        "same-actor": (CASE["proof-beta"], RKAF.proofIssuer, CASE["issuer-alpha"]),
+        "same-group": (
+            CASE["proof-beta"],
+            RKAF.independenceGroup,
+            CASE["group-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-response": (
+            CASE["proof-beta"],
+            RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact,
+            CASE["response-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-provider": (
+            CASE["issuer-beta"],
+            RKAF.proofResolver,
+            CASE["provider-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-model": (
+            CASE["lineage-beta"],
+            RKAF.modelId,
+            Literal("model-alpha"),
+        ),
+    }
+    for name, (subject, predicate, value) in axis_changes.items():
+        graph = _clone(base)
+        _replace(graph, subject, predicate, value)
+        cases[name] = (graph, {"independence"})
+
+    discarded = _clone(base)
+    _add_proof(discarded, "gamma", cite=False)
+    cases["discarded-support"] = (discarded, {"complete-support"})
+
+    replay = _clone(base)
+    replay.add((CASE.otherComparison, RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    replay.add((CASE.otherComparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome, RKAF.comparisonRefused))
+    replay.add(
+        (CASE.otherComparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, CASE["proof-alpha"])
+    )
+    cases["proof-replay"] = (replay, {"proof-replay"})
+
+    mixed_exact = _clone(base)
+    _replace(
+        mixed_exact,
+        CASE["proof-beta"],
+        RKAF.adjudicationVerdict,
+        RKAF.verdictNearSame,
+    )
+    cases["exact-with-near"] = (mixed_exact, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    valid_close = _clone(mixed_exact)
+    _replace(valid_close, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.closeMatch)
+    cases["valid-close"] = (valid_close, set())
+
+    close_without_near = _clone(base)
+    _replace(close_without_near, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.closeMatch)
+    cases["close-without-near"] = (close_without_near, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    branches = (
+        ("valid-broad", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetBroader, set()),
+        ("valid-narrow", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower, set()),
+        ("valid-related", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictRelated, set()),
+        ("broad-with-same", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+        ("narrow-with-same", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+        ("related-with-same", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+    )
+    for name, relation, verdict, expected in branches:
+        graph = _clone(base)
+        _replace(graph, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, relation)
+        for key in ("alpha", "beta"):
+            _replace(
+                graph,
+                CASE[f"proof-{key}"],
+                RKAF.adjudicationVerdict,
+                verdict,
+            )
+        cases[name] = (graph, expected)
+
+    unknown = _clone(base)
+    _replace(unknown, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, CASE.unsupportedRelation)
+    cases["unsupported-relation"] = (unknown, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    refused = _clone(mixed_exact)
+    _replace(
+        refused,
+        CASE.comparison,
+        RKAF.comparisonOutcome,
+        RKAF.comparisonRefused,
+    )
+    cases["refused-does-not-fold"] = (refused, set())
+    return cases
+
+
+def _run_case(kind: str, case_id: str, graph: Graph, expected: set[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
+    python = python_oracle(graph)
+    shacl = shape_oracle(graph)
+    if python != shacl or python != expected:
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"{kind}/{case_id}: expected={sorted(expected)}, "
+            f"python={sorted(python)}, shacl={sorted(shacl)}"
+        )
+    return {
+        "expected": sorted(expected),
+        "id": case_id,
+        "kind": kind,
+        "python": sorted(python),
+        "shacl": sorted(shacl),
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output",
+        type=Path,
+        default=ROOT / "research/move2/measurements.json",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    started = time.perf_counter()
+    results = [
+        _run_case("corpus", case_id, _fixture_graph(case_id), expected)
+        for case_id, expected in CORPUS_EXPECTED.items()
+    ]
+    results.extend(
+        _run_case("mutation", case_id, graph, expected)
+        for case_id, (graph, expected) in mutation_cases().items()
+    )
+    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
+    peak = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
+    peak_mib = peak / (1024 * 1024) if sys.platform == "darwin" else peak / 1024
+    summary = {
+        "corpusCases": sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
+        "corpusRuleChecks": 4 * sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
+        "elapsedSeconds": round(elapsed, 3),
+        "engine": "pySHACL 0.31.0",
+        "mutationCases": sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
+        "mutationRuleChecks": 4
+        * sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
+        "peakRssMiB": round(peak_mib, 1),
+        "results": results,
+        "status": "PASS",
+    }
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+    print(
+        f"move-2 oracle PASS: {summary['corpusCases']} corpus + "
+        f"{summary['mutationCases']} mutation cases in {summary['elapsedSeconds']}s; "
+        f"peak RSS {summary['peakRssMiB']} MiB"
+    )
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+def test_rulespec_shape_data_and_lock_are_part_of_contract_identity() -> None:

+            ]

+        )

+def test_copy_and_run_validator_imports_no_rulespec_or_refspec_package() -> None:
+    source = (BINDING / "tools" / "validate.py").read_text()
+    tree = ast.parse(source)
+    imported: set[str] = set()
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
+            imported.update(alias.name.split(".", 1)[0] for alias in node.names)
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
+            imported.add(node.module.split(".", 1)[0])
+    assert "refspec" not in imported
+    assert "rulespec_conformance" not in imported

    50	The other JSON files MUST validate against their correspondingly named schemas.
    51	Every schema uses JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 and is closed to unknown fields.
    52	
    53	The manifest pins the exact ontology, SHACL shapes, core JSON Schemas, validator
    54	version, every RDF pack, and all four supporting JSON files — in 3.1 that is
    55	the whole distribution, in one hop. Its `contractDigest` additionally
    56	covers a sorted path, length, and digest
    57	inventory of the ontology, shapes, every schema, registry profile map,
    58	coverage proof, and real-registry descriptor
    59	dataset and proof, so a supporting binding asset cannot change invisibly.
    60	
    61	`contractDigest` covers what conformance MEANS, and nothing else. The
    62	programs that read that meaning — `requirements.txt`, the fixture builder, the
    63	shared canonical RDF renderer, and this independent validator — are pinned
    64	separately and deliberately are NOT in it: folding them in made a one-line edit
    65	to a program reissue every fixture for a contract that had not moved. Which
    66	program produced a verdict is pinned by name and number instead, through the
    67	manifest's `binding.validatorVersion` and the acceptance record's `validator`
    68	name and version.
    69	
    70	Four relational adjudication rules are generated by the RuleSpec CUE
    71	compiler. They reach this copy-and-run binding as plain data in
    72	`shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl`; the validator still imports no
    73	RefSpec or RuleSpec Python package. The adjacent
    74	`shapes/rulespec-adjudication.lock.json` pins the source package version,
    75	source resource digests, and exact combined output. Both files participate in
    76	`contractDigest`, and both Atlas and RuleSpec shapes participate in
    77	`shapesDigest`. A maintainer with the intended `rulespec-conformance` wheel
    78	installed refreshes or checks the data with:
    79	
    80	```sh
    81	python tools/refresh_rulespec_adjudication_shapes.py
    82	python tools/refresh_rulespec_adjudication_shapes.py --check
    83	```
    84	
    85	The generator is a development tool. A copied binding executes only the local,
    86	digest-pinned Turtle.
    87	
    88	`fixtures/corpus.json` is not in it either, and for the same reason read the
    89	other way round: the conformance corpus is the PROOF that this validator
    90	behaves as the rules say, not one of the rules. While it sat in the contract
    91	digest, adding a single conformance case moved every manifest, acceptance
    92	record and construction summary on disk, breaking their external pins and
    93	invalidating a signed release for a contract that had not moved. Proof identity
    94	is recorded where the validation event is described instead: the acceptance
    95	record's `corpusDigest`, beside the `validator` identity it qualifies. A reader
    96	recomputes `contractDigest` from the binding on its own disk and refuses a
    97	disagreement; `corpusDigest` is recorded and never re-derived, so a grown

+COMPACT_OR_ABSOLUTE_IRI_RE = re.compile(
+    r"^(?:[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:[^\s]+|<[^\s<>]+>)$"
+)
+
+
+def parse_shacl_sparql_annotations(source: str) -> list[SparqlConstraintDef]:
+    """Parse the fail-closed CUE annotation format for graph rules.
+
+    The definition name supplies the stable shape local name. Its multiline
+    string has a generated-scaffolding header, a literal ``---`` separator,
+    then the SPARQL SELECT query::
+
+        #ExampleShapeSparql: <CUE multiline string>
+          targetClass: rkaf:Example
+          message: Explanation shown in a SHACL result.
+          ---
+          PREFIX rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#>
+          SELECT $this WHERE { ... }
+
+    Repeating ``targetClass`` is allowed. Everything else is rejected rather
+    than silently omitted from the emitted constraint.
+    """
+
+    constraints: list[SparqlConstraintDef] = []
+    seen: set[str] = set()
+    for match in SHACL_SPARQL_BLOCK_RE.finditer(source):
+        shape_name = match.group("shape")
+        if shape_name in seen:
+            raise CompileError(f"duplicate SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name}")
+        seen.add(shape_name)
+        header, separator, select = match.group("body").partition("\n---\n")
+        if not separator:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no --- query separator"
+            )
+        targets: list[str] = []
+        message: Optional[str] = None
+        for raw_line in header.splitlines():
+            line = raw_line.strip()
+            if not line:
+                continue
+            key, colon, value = line.partition(":")
+            if not colon or not value.strip():
+                raise CompileError(
+                    f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has malformed header {line!r}"
+                )
+            value = value.strip()
+            if key == "targetClass":
+                if not COMPACT_OR_ABSOLUTE_IRI_RE.fullmatch(value):
+                    raise CompileError(
+                        f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has invalid targetClass {value!r}"
+                    )
+                targets.append(value)
+            elif key == "message":
+                if message is not None:
+                    raise CompileError(
+                        f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} repeats message"
+                    )
+                message = value
+            else:
+                raise CompileError(
+                    f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has unknown header {key!r}"
+                )
+        query = select.strip()
+        if not targets:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no targetClass"
+            )
+        if not message:
+            raise CompileError(f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no message")
+        if not re.search(r"(?i)\bSELECT\s+(?:DISTINCT\s+)?\$this\b", query):
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} must SELECT $this"
+            )
+        if '"""' in query:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} contains a Turtle long-string terminator"
+            )
+        constraints.append(
+            SparqlConstraintDef(
+                shape_name=shape_name,
+                target_classes=targets,
+                message=message,
+                select=query,
+            )
+        )
+    return constraints
+

+# ---- SHACL-SPARQL target (annotated relational rules) --------------------
+
+def target_shacl_sparql(doc: ConstraintDoc) -> str:
+    """Emit only the relational rules explicitly carried by this CUE file."""
+
+    out: list[str] = [
+        "# AUTO-GENERATED by tools/constraints_compile.py "
+        "(target=shacl-sparql).",
+        "# Source: " + (
+            _source_relpath(doc.source_file) or str(doc.source_file or "unknown")
+        ),
+        "# DO NOT EDIT: change the #*ShapeSparql annotation in the CUE source.",
+        "",
+        "@prefix sh:   <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .",
+        "@prefix rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#> .",
+        "",
+    ]
+    for constraint in doc.sparql_constraints:
+        out.append(f"rkaf:{constraint.shape_name} a sh:NodeShape ;")
+        for target_class in constraint.target_classes:
+            out.append(f"  sh:targetClass {target_class} ;")
+        out.extend(
+            (
+                "  sh:sparql [",
+                "    a sh:SPARQLConstraint ;",
+                f"    sh:message {json.dumps(constraint.message)} ;",
+                '    sh:select """',
+                constraint.select,
+                '    """ ;',
+                "  ] .",
+                "",
+            )
+        )
+    return "\n".join(out)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Refresh the RuleSpec-owned adjudication shapes vendored into this binding.
+
+The binding validator deliberately imports no RefSpec or RuleSpec package
+code. This development-time generator is the only package-aware side of that
+boundary: it reads compiler output through the installed
+``rulespec_conformance.contract.resources`` accessor, writes plain Turtle
+beside the Atlas shapes, and records exact source and output digests.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from rulespec_conformance.contract import VERSION, resources
+
+BINDING_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+OUTPUT_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"
+LOCK_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.lock.json"
+RESOURCE_NAMES = ("machine-adjudication", "resolver-proof-record")
+
+
+def _digest(payload: bytes) -> str:
+    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _canonical_json(value: object) -> bytes:
+    return (
+        json.dumps(
+            value,
+            ensure_ascii=False,
+            allow_nan=False,
+            sort_keys=True,
+            separators=(",", ":"),
+        ).encode("utf-8")
+        + b"\n"
+    )
+
+
+def render() -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
+    parts = [
+        "# GENERATED by tools/refresh_rulespec_adjudication_shapes.py.",
+        "# Source: rulespec-conformance compiler output; do not edit here.",
+        f"# Rulespec contract version: {VERSION}",
+        "",
+    ]
+    source_rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
+    for name in RESOURCE_NAMES:
+        text = resources.shacl_sparql(name, family="analysis")
+        payload = text.encode("utf-8")
+        source_rows.append(
+            {
+                "accessor": (
+                    "rulespec_conformance.contract.resources."
+                    f"shacl_sparql({name!r}, family='analysis')"
+                ),
+                "byteLength": len(payload),
+                "digest": _digest(payload),
+                "name": name,
+            }
+        )
+        parts.extend((text.rstrip(), ""))
+    output = "\n".join(parts).encode("utf-8")
+    lock = _canonical_json(
+        {
+            "format": "RulespecAdjudicationShapeLock",
+            "formatVersion": "1.0",
+            "output": {
+                "byteLength": len(output),
+                "digest": _digest(output),
+                "path": "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl",
+            },
+            "package": "rulespec-conformance",
+            "packageVersion": VERSION,
+            "resources": source_rows,
+        }
+    )
+    return output, lock
+
+
+def _check(path: Path, expected: bytes) -> bool:
+    if not path.is_file():
+        print(f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} is missing")
+        return False
+    observed = path.read_bytes()
+    if observed != expected:
+        print(
+            f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} differs "
+            f"(expected {_digest(expected)}, found {_digest(observed)})"
+        )
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--check",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="refuse stale generated data instead of refreshing it",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    output, lock = render()
+    if args.check:
+        return 0 if _check(OUTPUT_PATH, output) and _check(LOCK_PATH, lock) else 1
+    OUTPUT_PATH.write_bytes(output)
+    LOCK_PATH.write_bytes(lock)
+    print(
+        "refreshed "
+        f"{OUTPUT_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} ({_digest(output)}) and "
+        f"{LOCK_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)}"
+    )
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+def _check_rulespec_shapes_lock() -> None:
+    """Verify the local compiler output against its package-provenance pin."""
+
+    lock = _load_json(RULESPEC_SHAPES_LOCK_PATH, require_canonical=True)
+    if not isinstance(lock, Mapping) or set(lock) != {
+        "format",
+        "formatVersion",
+        "output",
+        "package",
+        "packageVersion",
+        "resources",
+    }:
+        _fail("binding.rulespec-shapes", "RuleSpec shape lock is malformed")
+    if (
+        lock["format"] != "RulespecAdjudicationShapeLock"
+        or lock["formatVersion"] != "1.0"
+        or lock["package"] != "rulespec-conformance"
+        or not isinstance(lock["packageVersion"], str)
+        or not lock["packageVersion"]
+    ):
+        _fail("binding.rulespec-shapes", "RuleSpec shape lock identity differs")
+    output = lock["output"]
+    payload = RULESPEC_SHAPES_PATH.read_bytes()
+    if output != {
+        "byteLength": len(payload),
+        "digest": "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest(),
+        "path": "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl",
+    }:
+        _fail("binding.rulespec-shapes", "RuleSpec shape output differs from its lock")
+    resources = lock["resources"]
+    if (

+        )
+    ):
