+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Differential oracle for compiler-emitted adjudication SHACL-SPARQL.
+
+The Python implementation below is copied and reduced from the four relevant
+parts of ``bindings/atlas/3.1/tools/validate.py``. It deliberately imports
+neither that module nor RuleSpec compiler code: importing the implementation
+being replaced would make agreement circular.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import resource
+import sys
+import time
+from itertools import combinations
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from pyshacl import validate as shacl_validate
+from rdflib import Dataset, Graph, Literal, Namespace, URIRef
+from rdflib.namespace import RDF, SH, SKOS
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+BINDING = ROOT / "bindings/atlas/3.1"
+FIXTURES = BINDING / "fixtures"
+SHAPES_PATH = BINDING / "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"
+
+RKAF = Namespace("https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#")
+CASE = Namespace("urn:ref:move2-oracle:")
+
+RULE_SHAPES = {
+    "independence": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationFiveAxisIndependenceShape,
+    "complete-support": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationCompleteSupportShape,
+    "verdict-lattice": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationVerdictLatticeFoldShape,
+    "proof-replay": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationProofReplayShape,
+}
+
+CORPUS_EXPECTED = {
+    "adjudication-single-proof": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-validator-actor": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-independence-group": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-provider": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-provider-model": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-response-artifact": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-discarded-support": {"complete-support"},
+    "adjudication-relation-not-licensed": {"verdict-lattice"},
+    "adjudication-verdicts-disagree": {"verdict-lattice"},
+    "adjudication-foreign-comparison": {"proof-replay"},
+    "all-resource-profiles": set(),
+    "qualified-three-machine-support": set(),
+    "qualified-lattice-branches": set(),
+    "adjudication-refused-comparison-record": set(),
+}
+
+
+def _one(graph: Graph, subject: URIRef, predicate: URIRef) -> object:
+    values = list(graph.objects(subject, predicate))
+    if len(values) != 1:
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"oracle input requires one {predicate} on {subject}; found {len(values)}"
+        )
+    return values[0]
+
+
+def _fold_verdicts(verdicts: frozenset[object]) -> URIRef | None:
+    """Copied oracle for validate.py::_adjudicated_relation."""
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictSame}:
+        return SKOS.exactMatch
+    if verdicts <= {RKAF.verdictSame, RKAF.verdictNearSame} and (
+        RKAF.verdictNearSame in verdicts
+    ):
+        return SKOS.closeMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetBroader}:
+        return SKOS.broadMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower}:
+        return SKOS.narrowMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictRelated}:
+        return SKOS.relatedMatch
+    return None
+
+
+def python_oracle(graph: Graph) -> set[str]:
+    """Verdicts from the copied old Python behavior for the four rules."""
+    violations: set[str] = set()
+    comparisons = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    proofs = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.ResolverProofRecord))
+
+    for proof in proofs:
+        comparison = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofComparisonContext)
+        if proof not in set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord)):
+            violations.add("complete-support")
+        citing = {
+            subject
+            for subject in graph.subjects(RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, proof)
+            if subject in comparisons
+        }
+        if len(citing) > 1:
+            violations.add("proof-replay")
+
+    for comparison in comparisons:
+        if _one(graph, comparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome) != RKAF.comparisonSatisfied:
+            continue
+        cited = set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord))
+        facts: list[tuple[object, ...]] = []
+        for proof in cited:
+            issuer = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofIssuer)
+            lineage = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.hasAILineage)
+            facts.append(
+                (
+                    issuer,
+                    _one(graph, proof, RKAF.independenceGroup),
+                    _one(graph, issuer, RKAF.proofResolver),
+                    str(_one(graph, lineage, RKAF.modelId)),
+                    _one(graph, proof, RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact),
+                )
+            )
+        if not any(
+            all(left[index] != right[index] for index in range(5))
+            for left, right in combinations(facts, 2)
+        ):
+            violations.add("independence")
+
+        assertion = _one(graph, comparison, RKAF.comparisonExpectedAssertion)
+        stated_relation = _one(graph, assertion, RDF.predicate)
+        verdicts = frozenset(
+            _one(graph, proof, RKAF.adjudicationVerdict) for proof in cited
+        )
+        if _fold_verdicts(verdicts) != stated_relation:
+            violations.add("verdict-lattice")
+    return violations
+
+
+def shape_oracle(graph: Graph) -> set[str]:
+    """Run each emitted rule alone so its Boolean verdict has a stable ID."""
+    all_shapes = Graph().parse(SHAPES_PATH, format="turtle")
+    target_predicates = (
+        SH.targetClass,
+        SH.targetNode,
+        SH.targetSubjectsOf,
+        SH.targetObjectsOf,
+    )
+    violations: set[str] = set()
+    for rule, keep in RULE_SHAPES.items():
+        shapes = Graph()
+        for triple in all_shapes:
+            shapes.add(triple)
+        for predicate in target_predicates:
+            for subject, obj in list(shapes.subject_objects(predicate)):
+                if subject != keep:
+                    shapes.remove((subject, predicate, obj))
+        conforms, _, _ = shacl_validate(
+            graph,
+            shacl_graph=shapes,
+            inference="none",
+            advanced=True,
+            inplace=False,
+            abort_on_first=False,
+            meta_shacl=False,
+        )
+        if not conforms:
+            violations.add(rule)
+    return violations
+
+
+def _fixture_path(case_id: str) -> Path:
+    corpus = json.loads((FIXTURES / "corpus.json").read_bytes())
+    row = next(row for row in corpus["cases"] if row["id"] == case_id)
+    return FIXTURES / row["path"]
+
+
+def _fixture_graph(case_id: str) -> Graph:
+    root = _fixture_path(case_id)
+    if not root.is_dir():
+        raise SystemExit(
+            f"fixture {case_id} is not built; run "
+            "bindings/atlas/3.1/tools/build_fixtures.py first"
+        )
+    manifest = json.loads((root / "atlas-manifest.json").read_bytes())
+    asserted_id = URIRef(
+        next(row["id"] for row in manifest["graphs"] if row["role"] == "asserted")
+    )
+    dataset = Dataset()
+    for pack in manifest["packs"]:
+        payload = (root / pack["path"]).read_bytes()
+        if pack["transport"]["compression"] == "zstd":
+            try:
+                from compression import zstd
+            except ImportError:
+                from backports import zstd
+            payload = zstd.decompress(payload)
+        dataset.parse(data=payload.decode("utf-8"), format="nquads")
+    source = dataset.graph(asserted_id)
+    graph = Graph()
+    for triple in source:
+        graph.add(triple)
+    return graph
+
+
+def _add_proof(graph: Graph, key: str, *, cite: bool = True) -> URIRef:
+    proof = CASE[f"proof-{key}"]
+    issuer = CASE[f"issuer-{key}"]
+    lineage = CASE[f"lineage-{key}"]
+    graph.add((proof, RDF.type, RKAF.ResolverProofRecord))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.proofComparisonContext, CASE.comparison))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.proofIssuer, issuer))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.independenceGroup, CASE[f"group-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.hasAILineage, lineage))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact, CASE[f"response-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.adjudicationVerdict, RKAF.verdictSame))
+    graph.add((issuer, RKAF.proofResolver, CASE[f"provider-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((lineage, RKAF.modelId, Literal(f"model-{key}")))
+    if cite:
+        graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, proof))
+    return proof
+
+
+def _base_graph() -> Graph:
+    graph = Graph()
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome, RKAF.comparisonSatisfied))
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonExpectedAssertion, CASE.assertion))
+    graph.add((CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.exactMatch))
+    _add_proof(graph, "alpha")
+    _add_proof(graph, "beta")
+    return graph
+
+
+def _clone(graph: Graph) -> Graph:
+    result = Graph()
+    for triple in graph:
+        result.add(triple)
+    return result
+
+
+def _replace(graph: Graph, subject: URIRef, predicate: URIRef, value: object) -> None:
+    graph.remove((subject, predicate, None))
+    graph.add((subject, predicate, value))
+
+
+def mutation_cases() -> dict[str, tuple[Graph, set[str]]]:
+    base = _base_graph()
+    cases: dict[str, tuple[Graph, set[str]]] = {"valid-exact": (base, set())}
+
+    single = _clone(base)
+    single.remove((CASE["proof-beta"], None, None))
+    single.remove((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, CASE["proof-beta"]))
+    cases["single-proof"] = (single, {"independence"})
+
+    axis_changes = {
+        "same-actor": (CASE["proof-beta"], RKAF.proofIssuer, CASE["issuer-alpha"]),
+        "same-group": (
+            CASE["proof-beta"],
+            RKAF.independenceGroup,
+            CASE["group-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-response": (
+            CASE["proof-beta"],
+            RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact,
+            CASE["response-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-provider": (
+            CASE["issuer-beta"],
+            RKAF.proofResolver,
+            CASE["provider-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-model": (
+            CASE["lineage-beta"],
+            RKAF.modelId,
+            Literal("model-alpha"),
+        ),
+    }
+    for name, (subject, predicate, value) in axis_changes.items():
+        graph = _clone(base)
+        _replace(graph, subject, predicate, value)
+        cases[name] = (graph, {"independence"})
+
+    discarded = _clone(base)
+    _add_proof(discarded, "gamma", cite=False)
+    cases["discarded-support"] = (discarded, {"complete-support"})
+
+    replay = _clone(base)
+    replay.add((CASE.otherComparison, RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    replay.add((CASE.otherComparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome, RKAF.comparisonRefused))
+    replay.add(
+        (CASE.otherComparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, CASE["proof-alpha"])
+    )
+    cases["proof-replay"] = (replay, {"proof-replay"})
+
+    mixed_exact = _clone(base)
+    _replace(
+        mixed_exact,
+        CASE["proof-beta"],
+        RKAF.adjudicationVerdict,
+        RKAF.verdictNearSame,
+    )
+    cases["exact-with-near"] = (mixed_exact, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    valid_close = _clone(mixed_exact)
+    _replace(valid_close, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.closeMatch)
+    cases["valid-close"] = (valid_close, set())
+
+    close_without_near = _clone(base)
+    _replace(close_without_near, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.closeMatch)
+    cases["close-without-near"] = (close_without_near, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    branches = (
+        ("valid-broad", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetBroader, set()),
+        ("valid-narrow", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower, set()),
+        ("valid-related", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictRelated, set()),
+        ("broad-with-same", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+        ("narrow-with-same", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+        ("related-with-same", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+    )
+    for name, relation, verdict, expected in branches:
+        graph = _clone(base)
+        _replace(graph, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, relation)
+        for key in ("alpha", "beta"):
+            _replace(
+                graph,
+                CASE[f"proof-{key}"],
+                RKAF.adjudicationVerdict,
+                verdict,
+            )
+        cases[name] = (graph, expected)
+
+    unknown = _clone(base)
+    _replace(unknown, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, CASE.unsupportedRelation)
+    cases["unsupported-relation"] = (unknown, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    refused = _clone(mixed_exact)
+    _replace(
+        refused,
+        CASE.comparison,
+        RKAF.comparisonOutcome,
+        RKAF.comparisonRefused,
+    )
+    cases["refused-does-not-fold"] = (refused, set())
+    return cases
+
+
+def _run_case(kind: str, case_id: str, graph: Graph, expected: set[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
+    python = python_oracle(graph)
+    shacl = shape_oracle(graph)
+    if python != shacl or python != expected:
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"{kind}/{case_id}: expected={sorted(expected)}, "
+            f"python={sorted(python)}, shacl={sorted(shacl)}"
+        )
+    return {
+        "expected": sorted(expected),
+        "id": case_id,
+        "kind": kind,
+        "python": sorted(python),
+        "shacl": sorted(shacl),
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output",
+        type=Path,
+        default=ROOT / "research/move2/measurements.json",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    started = time.perf_counter()
+    results = [
+        _run_case("corpus", case_id, _fixture_graph(case_id), expected)
+        for case_id, expected in CORPUS_EXPECTED.items()
+    ]
+    results.extend(
+        _run_case("mutation", case_id, graph, expected)
+        for case_id, (graph, expected) in mutation_cases().items()
+    )
+    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
+    peak = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
+    peak_mib = peak / (1024 * 1024) if sys.platform == "darwin" else peak / 1024
+    summary = {
+        "corpusCases": sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
+        "corpusRuleChecks": 4 * sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
+        "elapsedSeconds": round(elapsed, 3),
+        "engine": "pySHACL 0.31.0",
+        "mutationCases": sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
+        "mutationRuleChecks": 4
+        * sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
+        "peakRssMiB": round(peak_mib, 1),
+        "results": results,
+        "status": "PASS",
+    }
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+    print(
+        f"move-2 oracle PASS: {summary['corpusCases']} corpus + "
+        f"{summary['mutationCases']} mutation cases in {summary['elapsedSeconds']}s; "
+        f"peak RSS {summary['peakRssMiB']} MiB"
+    )
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import ast
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from rdflib import URIRef
+from rdflib.namespace import RDF, SH
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+BINDING = ROOT / "bindings" / "atlas" / "3.1"
+sys.path.insert(0, str(BINDING / "tools"))
+import validate as atlas_validate
+
+EXPECTED_SHAPES = {
+    URIRef("https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#" + local)
+    for local in (
+        "MachineAdjudicationFiveAxisIndependenceShape",
+        "MachineAdjudicationCompleteSupportShape",
+        "MachineAdjudicationVerdictLatticeFoldShape",
+        "MachineAdjudicationProofReplayShape",
+    )
+}
+
+
+def test_binding_loads_the_four_compiler_emitted_shapes_as_local_data() -> None:
+    atlas_validate._check_rulespec_shapes_lock()
+    _, shapes = atlas_validate._parse_binding_graphs()
+    observed = set(shapes.subjects(RDF.type, SH.NodeShape))
+    assert EXPECTED_SHAPES <= observed
+
+
+def test_rulespec_shape_data_and_lock_are_part_of_contract_identity() -> None:
+    baseline = atlas_validate._binding_digests()["contractDigest"]
+    for relative in (
+        Path("shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"),
+        Path("shapes/rulespec-adjudication.lock.json"),
+    ):
+        changed = (BINDING / relative).read_bytes() + b"\n"
+        assert (
+            atlas_validate._binding_digests(content_overrides={relative: changed})[
+                "contractDigest"
+            ]
+            != baseline
+        )
+
+
+def test_copy_and_run_validator_imports_no_rulespec_or_refspec_package() -> None:
+    source = (BINDING / "tools" / "validate.py").read_text()
+    tree = ast.parse(source)
+    imported: set[str] = set()
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
+            imported.update(alias.name.split(".", 1)[0] for alias in node.names)
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
+            imported.add(node.module.split(".", 1)[0])
+    assert "refspec" not in imported
+    assert "rulespec_conformance" not in imported

 succeeded in 0ms:
   210	# ── Analysis §4.3 — a proof is bound to the comparison that cites it ─────────
   211	#
   212	# `rkaf:proofComparisonContext` is REQUIRED on every `#ResolverProofRecord`,
   213	# and §4.3 says why: "a proof that does not name its comparison can be replayed
   214	# against a different one, which is how a stale pass gets reused". Requiring the
   215	# property only makes the binding DECLARED. Nothing per-property can check that
   216	# the named comparison is the one actually citing the proof, because that is a
   217	# statement relating two nodes.
   218	#
   219	# Without this shape a producer could take a 2019 gate pass, cite it from a 2026
   220	# comparison, and leave `rkaf:proofComparisonContext` pointing at the 2019
   221	# context: every per-property constraint passes, and a stale pass backs a fresh
   222	# discrepancy finding. `rkaf:proofRecordDigest` does not catch it either — the
   223	# proof record is unedited; it is the CITATION that is fraudulent.
   224	#
   225	# Written to fire only when the proof node is present in the graph and names a
   226	# comparison, so a comparison published alone, with its proofs dereferenced
   227	# elsewhere, validates exactly as it did before.
   228	rkaf:ResolverProofComparisonBindingShape a sh:NodeShape ;
   229	  sh:targetClass rkaf:RelationComparisonContext ;
   230	  sh:sparql [
   231	    a sh:SPARQLConstraint ;
   232	    sh:message "A rkaf:ResolverProofRecord cited by rkaf:comparisonProofRecord MUST name that same rkaf:RelationComparisonContext in rkaf:proofComparisonContext. A proof issued for another comparison is a replayed, possibly stale, pass (spec/rkaf-analysis.md §4.3)." ;
   233	    sh:select """
   234	      PREFIX rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#>
   235	      SELECT $this
   236	      WHERE {
   237	        $this rkaf:comparisonProofRecord ?proof .
   238	        ?proof rkaf:proofComparisonContext ?other .
   239	        FILTER (?other != $this)
   240	      }
   241	    """ ;
   242	  ] .
   243	
   244	# ── Analysis §4 extension — machine-adjudication proofs ARE resolver proofs ──
   245	#
   246	# A machine-adjudication proof (`constraints/analysis/machine-adjudication.cue`,
   247	# `#MachineAdjudicationProof`) is NOT a second `@type`. It is a plain
   248	# `rkaf:ResolverProofRecord` whose `rkaf:proofType` equals the literal
   249	# `rkaf:machineAdjudicationProof`: two structs declaring the same `@type`
   250	# literal would collide in `tools/conformance_lib.py::schema_bindings()`
   251	# (exactly one compiled schema may validate a given `@type`), and an
   252	# `rdfs:subClassOf`-related second `@type` does not help either — the SHACL
   253	# `sh:class` constraint component does not apply RDFS subclass entailment the
   254	# way `sh:targetClass` does without an explicitly supplied `ont_graph`, and
   255	# `tools/ci_validate.py` never supplies one. So the two shapes below find a
   256	# machine-adjudication proof by its `rkaf:proofType` value, never by `rdf:type`,
   257	# and every cross-node rule that already reasons over `rkaf:ResolverProofRecord`
   258	# — `sh:class` on `rkaf:comparisonProofRecord` / `rkaf:findingProofRecord`, and
   259	# `rkaf:ResolverProofComparisonBindingShape` above — applies to it for free,
   260	# because it always was one.
   261	
   262	# ── Machine adjudication — at least one independent pair ─────────────────────
   263	#
   264	# Analysis §4 extension (machine-adjudication.cue) says a model MAY produce a
   265	# machine-adjudication proof, but no model decides a comparison OUTCOME alone
   266	# (spec/rkaf-analysis.md §3.4). What makes that true in the graph, not only in
   267	# prose, is this rule: among the machine-adjudication proofs a claim cites — a
   268	# `rkaf:RelationComparisonContext` via `rkaf:comparisonProofRecord`, or a
   269	# `rkaf:RelationFinding` via `rkaf:findingProofRecord` — at least one PAIR must
   270	# answer the identical sealed question (`rkaf:sealedRequestDigest` equal) while
   271	# being genuinely independent witnesses of it: distinct on all five of
   272	# `rkaf:proofIssuer` (validator actor), `rkaf:independenceGroup`,
   273	# `rkaf:proofIssuer -> rkaf:proofResolver` (provider),
   274	# `rkaf:hasAILineage -> rkaf:modelId` (provider model ID), and
   275	# `rkaf:sealedResponseArtifact` (response artifact). A single
   276	# machine-adjudication proof, or a set that collapses onto one axis, is one
   277	# opinion wearing a proof record. The fifth axis (spec/rkaf-refspec.md,
   278	# corrected 2026-08-09) keeps two "independent" machines from qualifying a
   279	# pair by each sealing the same shared response: distinct issuers, groups,
   280	# providers, and model IDs still describe one witnessed answer if that answer
   281	# is the identical sealed artifact.
   282	#
   283	# `rkaf:sealedResponseArtifact` names the sealed RECORD of that proof's own
   284	# run, not the response bytes it contains: artifact-IRI inequality is a
   285	# producer promise, not a content check. A producer MUST mint a distinct
   286	# per-run artifact for every adjudication call even when two genuinely
   287	# independent runs return byte-identical output (run identity, not content
   288	# identity) — the same way `rkaf:Artifact` may itself be content-addressed
   289	# (`rkaf:cid`, `rkaf:hash-sha256`; spec/rkaf-core.md §4.1) without that making
   290	# two separately-fetched copies of one document into two documents. Two
   291	# proofs naming the SAME `rkaf:sealedResponseArtifact` are read as one
   292	# response copied onto a second proof record, never as two independent
   293	# witnesses that happened to agree byte-for-byte.
   294	#
   295	# This SPARQL enforces artifact-IRI distinctness, which is necessary but not
   296	# sufficient on its own: `rkaf:sealedResponseArtifact` carries at most one
   297	# value per proof (`compiled/shacl/analysis/resolver-proof-record.ttl`,
   298	# generated from the `rkaf:machineAdjudicationProof` conditional in
   299	# `constraints/analysis/resolver-proof-record.cue`) precisely so a proof
   300	# cannot carry both a shared artifact and a distinct decoy one and pass this
   301	# rule on the decoy.
   302	#
   303	# This corrects rulespec's own prior wording (spec/rkaf-analysis.md §4
   304	# extension, corrected 2026-08-09): the requirement is AT LEAST ONE independent
   305	# pair, not EXACTLY
   306	# TWO proofs. The stricter "exactly two" rule was wrong on its own terms: it
   307	# would reject a valid three-machine corroboration, discarding a third witness
   308	# that helped establish the relation, which is the opposite of what an
   309	# independence requirement is for. The companion
   310	# `rkaf:MachineAdjudicationCompleteSupportShape` below is the other half of
   311	# that correction — this shape proves independence exists; that one proves
   312	# nothing corroborating was thrown away to manufacture it.
   313	#
   314	# Fires only when at least one cited proof's `rkaf:proofType` is
   315	# `rkaf:machineAdjudicationProof`, so a claim resting on other resolver
   316	# protocols entirely is untouched.
   317	rkaf:MachineAdjudicationIndependentPairShape a sh:NodeShape ;
   318	  sh:targetClass rkaf:RelationComparisonContext ;
   319	  sh:targetClass rkaf:RelationFinding ;
   320	  sh:sparql [
   321	    a sh:SPARQLConstraint ;
   322	    sh:message "A claim citing any rkaf:ResolverProofRecord whose rkaf:proofType is rkaf:machineAdjudicationProof MUST cite at least one PAIR of them that share rkaf:sealedRequestDigest and are distinct on all five independence axes: rkaf:proofIssuer (validator actor), rkaf:independenceGroup, rkaf:proofIssuer/rkaf:proofResolver (provider), rkaf:hasAILineage/rkaf:modelId (provider model ID), and rkaf:sealedResponseArtifact (response artifact). A single machine adjudication, or a set that collapses onto one axis, is one opinion, not independent corroboration (spec/rkaf-analysis.md §3.4, §4 extension; spec/rkaf-refspec.md, corrected 2026-08-09)." ;
   323	    sh:select """
   324	      PREFIX rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#>
   325	      SELECT DISTINCT $this
   326	      WHERE {
   327	        {
   328	          { $this rkaf:comparisonProofRecord ?proof }
   329	          UNION
   330	          { $this rkaf:findingProofRecord ?proof }
   331	        }
   332	        ?proof rkaf:proofType rkaf:machineAdjudicationProof .
   333	        FILTER NOT EXISTS {
   334	          {
   335	            { $this rkaf:comparisonProofRecord ?p1 }
   336	            UNION
   337	            { $this rkaf:findingProofRecord ?p1 }
   338	          }
   339	          {
   340	            { $this rkaf:comparisonProofRecord ?p2 }
   341	            UNION
   342	            { $this rkaf:findingProofRecord ?p2 }
   343	          }
   344	          ?p1 rkaf:proofType rkaf:machineAdjudicationProof .
   345	          ?p2 rkaf:proofType rkaf:machineAdjudicationProof .
   346	          FILTER (?p1 != ?p2)
   347	          ?p1 rkaf:sealedRequestDigest ?digest .
   348	          ?p2 rkaf:sealedRequestDigest ?digest .
   349	          ?p1 rkaf:proofIssuer ?actor1 .
   350	          ?p2 rkaf:proofIssuer ?actor2 .
   351	          FILTER (?actor1 != ?actor2)
   352	          ?p1 rkaf:independenceGroup ?group1 .
   353	          ?p2 rkaf:independenceGroup ?group2 .
   354	          FILTER (?group1 != ?group2)
   355	          ?actor1 rkaf:proofResolver ?provider1 .
   356	          ?actor2 rkaf:proofResolver ?provider2 .
   357	          FILTER (?provider1 != ?provider2)
   358	          ?p1 rkaf:hasAILineage ?lineage1 .
   359	          ?p2 rkaf:hasAILineage ?lineage2 .
   360	          ?lineage1 rkaf:modelId ?model1 .
   361	          ?lineage2 rkaf:modelId ?model2 .
   362	          FILTER (?model1 != ?model2)
   363	          ?p1 rkaf:sealedResponseArtifact ?artifact1 .
   364	          ?p2 rkaf:sealedResponseArtifact ?artifact2 .
   365	          FILTER (?artifact1 != ?artifact2)
   366	        }
   367	      }
   368	    """ ;
   369	  ] .
   370	
   371	# ── Machine adjudication — complete support retained ──────────────────────────
   372	#
   373	# The companion half of the independence rule above. A claim MUST cite the
   374	# complete set of machine-adjudication proofs that supported it, once
   375	# qualification runs: publishing only the first independent pair and quietly
   376	# dropping a third, fourth, or later machine that answered the SAME sealed
   377	# question discards evidence that helped determine the relation, even though
   378	# independence alone would already be satisfied by the pair kept
   379	# (spec/rkaf-analysis.md §4 extension, corrected 2026-08-09).
   380	#
   381	# Per-property SHACL cannot reach this: nothing about ONE cited proof record is
   382	# wrong, and the defect is a proof that self-declares support for this claim
   383	# (`rkaf:proofComparisonContext` naming `$this`, exactly the declared half of
   384	# `rkaf:ResolverProofComparisonBindingShape`) yet is absent from the citing
   385	# list. `rkaf:proofRecordDigest` cannot catch it either — the discarded proof
   386	# is untouched; it is the claim's citation list that is incomplete.
   387	#
   388	# Scoped to `rkaf:RelationComparisonContext` only: a machine-adjudication proof
   389	# declares the comparison it was issued for via `rkaf:proofComparisonContext`,
   390	# and no analogous self-declaring edge exists from a proof back to a
   391	# `rkaf:RelationFinding`, so there is nothing for this direction of the rule to
   392	# read on that class.
   393	rkaf:MachineAdjudicationCompleteSupportShape a sh:NodeShape ;
   394	  sh:targetClass rkaf:RelationComparisonContext ;
   395	  sh:sparql [
   396	    a sh:SPARQLConstraint ;
   397	    sh:message "A rkaf:ResolverProofRecord whose rkaf:proofType is rkaf:machineAdjudicationProof, that declares rkaf:proofComparisonContext naming this comparison and shares rkaf:sealedRequestDigest with a proof this comparison DOES cite, MUST also be cited by rkaf:comparisonProofRecord. Discarding a corroborating machine-adjudication proof loses evidence (spec/rkaf-analysis.md §4 extension)." ;
   398	    sh:select """
   399	      PREFIX rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#>
   400	      SELECT DISTINCT $this
   401	      WHERE {
   402	        $this rkaf:comparisonProofRecord ?cited .
   403	        ?cited rkaf:proofType rkaf:machineAdjudicationProof ;
   404	               rkaf:sealedRequestDigest ?digest .
   405	        ?discarded rkaf:proofType rkaf:machineAdjudicationProof ;
   406	                   rkaf:proofComparisonContext $this ;
   407	                   rkaf:sealedRequestDigest ?digest .
   408	        FILTER NOT EXISTS { $this rkaf:comparisonProofRecord ?discarded }
   409	      }
   410	    """ ;
   411	  ] .

+SHACL_SPARQL_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(
+    r'(?ms)^#(?P<shape>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*Shape)Sparql:\s*"""\n'
+    r'(?P<body>.*?)\n"""\s*$'
+)
+COMPACT_OR_ABSOLUTE_IRI_RE = re.compile(
+    r"^(?:[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:[^\s]+|<[^\s<>]+>)$"
+)
+
+
+def parse_shacl_sparql_annotations(source: str) -> list[SparqlConstraintDef]:
+    """Parse the fail-closed CUE annotation format for graph rules.
+
+    The definition name supplies the stable shape local name. Its multiline
+    string has a generated-scaffolding header, a literal ``---`` separator,
+    then the SPARQL SELECT query::
+
+        #ExampleShapeSparql: <CUE multiline string>
+          targetClass: rkaf:Example
+          message: Explanation shown in a SHACL result.
+          ---
+          PREFIX rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#>
+          SELECT $this WHERE { ... }
+
+    Repeating ``targetClass`` is allowed. Everything else is rejected rather
+    than silently omitted from the emitted constraint.
+    """
+
+    constraints: list[SparqlConstraintDef] = []
+    seen: set[str] = set()
+    for match in SHACL_SPARQL_BLOCK_RE.finditer(source):
+        shape_name = match.group("shape")
+        if shape_name in seen:
+            raise CompileError(f"duplicate SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name}")
+        seen.add(shape_name)
+        header, separator, select = match.group("body").partition("\n---\n")
+        if not separator:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no --- query separator"
+            )
+        targets: list[str] = []
+        message: Optional[str] = None
+        for raw_line in header.splitlines():
+            line = raw_line.strip()
+            if not line:
+                continue
+            key, colon, value = line.partition(":")
+            if not colon or not value.strip():
+                raise CompileError(
+                    f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has malformed header {line!r}"
+                )
+            value = value.strip()
+            if key == "targetClass":
+                if not COMPACT_OR_ABSOLUTE_IRI_RE.fullmatch(value):
+                    raise CompileError(
+                        f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has invalid targetClass {value!r}"
+                    )
+                targets.append(value)
+            elif key == "message":
+                if message is not None:
+                    raise CompileError(
+                        f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} repeats message"
+                    )
+                message = value
+            else:
+                raise CompileError(
+                    f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has unknown header {key!r}"
+                )
+        query = select.strip()
+        if not targets:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no targetClass"
+            )
+        if not message:
+            raise CompileError(f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no message")
+        if not re.search(r"(?i)\bSELECT\s+(?:DISTINCT\s+)?\$this\b", query):
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} must SELECT $this"
+            )
+        if '"""' in query:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} contains a Turtle long-string terminator"
+            )
+        constraints.append(
+            SparqlConstraintDef(
+                shape_name=shape_name,
+                target_classes=targets,
+                message=message,
+                select=query,
+            )
+        )
+    return constraints
+

+# ---- SHACL-SPARQL target (annotated relational rules) --------------------
+
+def target_shacl_sparql(doc: ConstraintDoc) -> str:
+    """Emit only the relational rules explicitly carried by this CUE file."""
+
+    out: list[str] = [
+        "# AUTO-GENERATED by tools/constraints_compile.py "
+        "(target=shacl-sparql).",
+        "# Source: " + (
+            _source_relpath(doc.source_file) or str(doc.source_file or "unknown")
+        ),
+        "# DO NOT EDIT: change the #*ShapeSparql annotation in the CUE source.",
+        "",
+        "@prefix sh:   <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .",
+        "@prefix rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#> .",
+        "",
+    ]
+    for constraint in doc.sparql_constraints:
+        out.append(f"rkaf:{constraint.shape_name} a sh:NodeShape ;")
+        for target_class in constraint.target_classes:
+            out.append(f"  sh:targetClass {target_class} ;")
+        out.extend(
+            (
+                "  sh:sparql [",
+                "    a sh:SPARQLConstraint ;",
+                f"    sh:message {json.dumps(constraint.message)} ;",
+                '    sh:select """',
+                constraint.select,
+                '    """ ;',
+                "  ] .",
+                "",
+            )
+        )
+    return "\n".join(out)

+    def test_four_relational_rules_are_emitted_as_parseable_shacl(self) -> None:
+        graph = Graph()
+        observed: set[URIRef] = set()
+        for source in self.SOURCES:
+            document = parse_cue_file(source)
+            turtle = target_shacl_sparql(document)
+            self.assertNotIn("sh:sparql", target_shacl(document))
+            graph.parse(data=turtle, format="turtle")
+            observed.update(
+                subject
+                for subject in graph.subjects(RDF.type, SH.NodeShape)
+                if str(subject).startswith("https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#")
+            )

+                "MachineAdjudicationCompleteSupportShape",
+                "MachineAdjudicationVerdictLatticeFoldShape",
+                "MachineAdjudicationProofReplayShape",
+            )
+        }

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Refresh the RuleSpec-owned adjudication shapes vendored into this binding.
+
+The binding validator deliberately imports no RefSpec or RuleSpec package
+code. This development-time generator is the only package-aware side of that
+boundary: it reads compiler output through the installed
+``rulespec_conformance.contract.resources`` accessor, writes plain Turtle
+beside the Atlas shapes, and records exact source and output digests.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from rulespec_conformance.contract import VERSION, resources
+
+BINDING_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+OUTPUT_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"
+LOCK_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.lock.json"
+RESOURCE_NAMES = ("machine-adjudication", "resolver-proof-record")
+
+
+def _digest(payload: bytes) -> str:
+    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _canonical_json(value: object) -> bytes:
+    return (
+        json.dumps(
+            value,
+            ensure_ascii=False,
+            allow_nan=False,
+            sort_keys=True,
+            separators=(",", ":"),
+        ).encode("utf-8")
+        + b"\n"
+    )
+
+
+def render() -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
+    parts = [
+        "# GENERATED by tools/refresh_rulespec_adjudication_shapes.py.",
+        "# Source: rulespec-conformance compiler output; do not edit here.",
+        f"# Rulespec contract version: {VERSION}",
+        "",
+    ]
+    source_rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
+    for name in RESOURCE_NAMES:
+        text = resources.shacl_sparql(name, family="analysis")
+        payload = text.encode("utf-8")
+        source_rows.append(
+            {
+                "accessor": (
+                    "rulespec_conformance.contract.resources."
+                    f"shacl_sparql({name!r}, family='analysis')"
+                ),
+                "byteLength": len(payload),
+                "digest": _digest(payload),
+                "name": name,
+            }
+        )
+        parts.extend((text.rstrip(), ""))
+    output = "\n".join(parts).encode("utf-8")
+    lock = _canonical_json(
+        {
+            "format": "RulespecAdjudicationShapeLock",
+            "formatVersion": "1.0",
+            "output": {
+                "byteLength": len(output),
+                "digest": _digest(output),
+                "path": "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl",
+            },
+            "package": "rulespec-conformance",
+            "packageVersion": VERSION,
+            "resources": source_rows,
+        }
+    )
+    return output, lock
+
+
+def _check(path: Path, expected: bytes) -> bool:
+    if not path.is_file():
+        print(f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} is missing")
+        return False
+    observed = path.read_bytes()
+    if observed != expected:
+        print(
+            f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} differs "
+            f"(expected {_digest(expected)}, found {_digest(observed)})"
+        )
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--check",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="refuse stale generated data instead of refreshing it",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    output, lock = render()
+    if args.check:
+        return 0 if _check(OUTPUT_PATH, output) and _check(LOCK_PATH, lock) else 1
+    OUTPUT_PATH.write_bytes(output)
+    LOCK_PATH.write_bytes(lock)
+    print(
+        "refreshed "
+        f"{OUTPUT_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} ({_digest(output)}) and "
+        f"{LOCK_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)}"
+    )
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Differential oracle for compiler-emitted adjudication SHACL-SPARQL.
+
+The Python implementation below is copied and reduced from the four relevant
+parts of ``bindings/atlas/3.1/tools/validate.py``. It deliberately imports
+neither that module nor RuleSpec compiler code: importing the implementation
+being replaced would make agreement circular.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import resource
+import sys
+import time
+from itertools import combinations
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from pyshacl import validate as shacl_validate
+from rdflib import Dataset, Graph, Literal, Namespace, URIRef
+from rdflib.namespace import RDF, SH, SKOS
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+BINDING = ROOT / "bindings/atlas/3.1"
+FIXTURES = BINDING / "fixtures"
+SHAPES_PATH = BINDING / "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"
+
+RKAF = Namespace("https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#")
+CASE = Namespace("urn:ref:move2-oracle:")
+
+RULE_SHAPES = {
+    "independence": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationFiveAxisIndependenceShape,
+    "complete-support": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationCompleteSupportShape,
+    "verdict-lattice": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationVerdictLatticeFoldShape,
+    "proof-replay": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationProofReplayShape,
+}
+
+CORPUS_EXPECTED = {
+    "adjudication-single-proof": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-validator-actor": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-independence-group": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-provider": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-provider-model": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-response-artifact": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-discarded-support": {"complete-support"},
+    "adjudication-relation-not-licensed": {"verdict-lattice"},
+    "adjudication-verdicts-disagree": {"verdict-lattice"},
+    "adjudication-foreign-comparison": {"proof-replay"},
+    "all-resource-profiles": set(),
+    "qualified-three-machine-support": set(),
+    "qualified-lattice-branches": set(),
+    "adjudication-refused-comparison-record": set(),
+}
+
+
+def _one(graph: Graph, subject: URIRef, predicate: URIRef) -> object:
+    values = list(graph.objects(subject, predicate))
+    if len(values) != 1:
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"oracle input requires one {predicate} on {subject}; found {len(values)}"
+        )
+    return values[0]
+
+
+def _fold_verdicts(verdicts: frozenset[object]) -> URIRef | None:
+    """Copied oracle for validate.py::_adjudicated_relation."""
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictSame}:
+        return SKOS.exactMatch
+    if verdicts <= {RKAF.verdictSame, RKAF.verdictNearSame} and (
+        RKAF.verdictNearSame in verdicts
+    ):
+        return SKOS.closeMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetBroader}:
+        return SKOS.broadMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower}:
+        return SKOS.narrowMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictRelated}:
+        return SKOS.relatedMatch
+    return None
+
+
+def python_oracle(graph: Graph) -> set[str]:
+    """Verdicts from the copied old Python behavior for the four rules."""
+    violations: set[str] = set()
+    comparisons = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    proofs = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.ResolverProofRecord))
+
+    for proof in proofs:
+        comparison = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofComparisonContext)
+        if proof not in set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord)):
+            violations.add("complete-support")
+        citing = {
+            subject
+            for subject in graph.subjects(RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, proof)
+            if subject in comparisons
+        }
+        if len(citing) > 1:
+            violations.add("proof-replay")
+
+    for comparison in comparisons:
+        if _one(graph, comparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome) != RKAF.comparisonSatisfied:
+            continue
+        cited = set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord))
+        facts: list[tuple[object, ...]] = []
+        for proof in cited:
+            issuer = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofIssuer)
+            lineage = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.hasAILineage)
+            facts.append(
+                (
+                    issuer,
+                    _one(graph, proof, RKAF.independenceGroup),
+                    _one(graph, issuer, RKAF.proofResolver),
+                    str(_one(graph, lineage, RKAF.modelId)),
+                    _one(graph, proof, RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact),
+                )
+            )
+        if not any(
+            all(left[index] != right[index] for index in range(5))
+            for left, right in combinations(facts, 2)
+        ):
+            violations.add("independence")
+
+        assertion = _one(graph, comparison, RKAF.comparisonExpectedAssertion)
+        stated_relation = _one(graph, assertion, RDF.predicate)
+        verdicts = frozenset(
+            _one(graph, proof, RKAF.adjudicationVerdict) for proof in cited
+        )
+        if _fold_verdicts(verdicts) != stated_relation:
+            violations.add("verdict-lattice")
+    return violations
+
+
+def shape_oracle(graph: Graph) -> set[str]:
+    """Run each emitted rule alone so its Boolean verdict has a stable ID."""
+    all_shapes = Graph().parse(SHAPES_PATH, format="turtle")
+    target_predicates = (
+        SH.targetClass,
+        SH.targetNode,
+        SH.targetSubjectsOf,
+        SH.targetObjectsOf,
+    )
+    violations: set[str] = set()
+    for rule, keep in RULE_SHAPES.items():
+        shapes = Graph()
+        for triple in all_shapes:
+            shapes.add(triple)
+        for predicate in target_predicates:
+            for subject, obj in list(shapes.subject_objects(predicate)):
+                if subject != keep:
+                    shapes.remove((subject, predicate, obj))
+        conforms, _, _ = shacl_validate(
+            graph,
+            shacl_graph=shapes,
+            inference="none",
+            advanced=True,
+            inplace=False,
+            abort_on_first=False,
+            meta_shacl=False,
+        )
+        if not conforms:
+            violations.add(rule)
+    return violations
+
+
+def _fixture_path(case_id: str) -> Path:
+    corpus = json.loads((FIXTURES / "corpus.json").read_bytes())
+    row = next(row for row in corpus["cases"] if row["id"] == case_id)
+    return FIXTURES / row["path"]
+
+
+def _fixture_graph(case_id: str) -> Graph:
+    root = _fixture_path(case_id)
+    if not root.is_dir():
+        raise SystemExit(
+            f"fixture {case_id} is not built; run "
+            "bindings/atlas/3.1/tools/build_fixtures.py first"
+        )
+    manifest = json.loads((root / "atlas-manifest.json").read_bytes())
+    asserted_id = URIRef(
+        next(row["id"] for row in manifest["graphs"] if row["role"] == "asserted")
+    )
+    dataset = Dataset()
+    for pack in manifest["packs"]:
+        payload = (root / pack["path"]).read_bytes()
+        if pack["transport"]["compression"] == "zstd":
+            try:
+                from compression import zstd
+            except ImportError:
+                from backports import zstd
+            payload = zstd.decompress(payload)
+        dataset.parse(data=payload.decode("utf-8"), format="nquads")
+    source = dataset.graph(asserted_id)
+    graph = Graph()
+    for triple in source:
+        graph.add(triple)
+    return graph
+
+
+def _add_proof(graph: Graph, key: str, *, cite: bool = True) -> URIRef:
+    proof = CASE[f"proof-{key}"]
+    issuer = CASE[f"issuer-{key}"]
+    lineage = CASE[f"lineage-{key}"]
+    graph.add((proof, RDF.type, RKAF.ResolverProofRecord))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.proofComparisonContext, CASE.comparison))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.proofIssuer, issuer))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.independenceGroup, CASE[f"group-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.hasAILineage, lineage))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact, CASE[f"response-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.adjudicationVerdict, RKAF.verdictSame))
+    graph.add((issuer, RKAF.proofResolver, CASE[f"provider-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((lineage, RKAF.modelId, Literal(f"model-{key}")))
+    if cite:
+        graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, proof))
+    return proof
+
+
+def _base_graph() -> Graph:
+    graph = Graph()
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome, RKAF.comparisonSatisfied))
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonExpectedAssertion, CASE.assertion))
+    graph.add((CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.exactMatch))
+    _add_proof(graph, "alpha")
+    _add_proof(graph, "beta")
+    return graph
+
+
+def _clone(graph: Graph) -> Graph:
+    result = Graph()
+    for triple in graph:
+        result.add(triple)
+    return result
+
+
+def _replace(graph: Graph, subject: URIRef, predicate: URIRef, value: object) -> None:
+    graph.remove((subject, predicate, None))
+    graph.add((subject, predicate, value))
+
+
+def mutation_cases() -> dict[str, tuple[Graph, set[str]]]:
+    base = _base_graph()
+    cases: dict[str, tuple[Graph, set[str]]] = {"valid-exact": (base, set())}
+
+    single = _clone(base)
+    single.remove((CASE["proof-beta"], None, None))
+    single.remove((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, CASE["proof-beta"]))
+    cases["single-proof"] = (single, {"independence"})
+
+    axis_changes = {
+        "same-actor": (CASE["proof-beta"], RKAF.proofIssuer, CASE["issuer-alpha"]),
+        "same-group": (
+            CASE["proof-beta"],
+            RKAF.independenceGroup,
+            CASE["group-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-response": (
+            CASE["proof-beta"],
+            RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact,
+            CASE["response-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-provider": (
+            CASE["issuer-beta"],
+            RKAF.proofResolver,
+            CASE["provider-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-model": (
+            CASE["lineage-beta"],
+            RKAF.modelId,
+            Literal("model-alpha"),
+        ),
+    }
+    for name, (subject, predicate, value) in axis_changes.items():
+        graph = _clone(base)
+        _replace(graph, subject, predicate, value)
+        cases[name] = (graph, {"independence"})
+
+    discarded = _clone(base)
+    _add_proof(discarded, "gamma", cite=False)
+    cases["discarded-support"] = (discarded, {"complete-support"})
+
+    replay = _clone(base)
+    replay.add((CASE.otherComparison, RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    replay.add((CASE.otherComparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome, RKAF.comparisonRefused))
+    replay.add(
+        (CASE.otherComparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, CASE["proof-alpha"])
+    )
+    cases["proof-replay"] = (replay, {"proof-replay"})
+
+    mixed_exact = _clone(base)
+    _replace(
+        mixed_exact,
+        CASE["proof-beta"],
+        RKAF.adjudicationVerdict,
+        RKAF.verdictNearSame,
+    )
+    cases["exact-with-near"] = (mixed_exact, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    valid_close = _clone(mixed_exact)
+    _replace(valid_close, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.closeMatch)
+    cases["valid-close"] = (valid_close, set())
+
+    close_without_near = _clone(base)
+    _replace(close_without_near, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.closeMatch)
+    cases["close-without-near"] = (close_without_near, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    branches = (
+        ("valid-broad", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetBroader, set()),
+        ("valid-narrow", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower, set()),
+        ("valid-related", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictRelated, set()),
+        ("broad-with-same", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+        ("narrow-with-same", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+        ("related-with-same", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+    )
+    for name, relation, verdict, expected in branches:
+        graph = _clone(base)
+        _replace(graph, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, relation)
+        for key in ("alpha", "beta"):
+            _replace(
+                graph,
+                CASE[f"proof-{key}"],
+                RKAF.adjudicationVerdict,
+                verdict,
+            )
+        cases[name] = (graph, expected)
+
+    unknown = _clone(base)
+    _replace(unknown, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, CASE.unsupportedRelation)
+    cases["unsupported-relation"] = (unknown, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    refused = _clone(mixed_exact)
+    _replace(
+        refused,
+        CASE.comparison,
+        RKAF.comparisonOutcome,
+        RKAF.comparisonRefused,
+    )
+    cases["refused-does-not-fold"] = (refused, set())
+    return cases
+
+
+def _run_case(kind: str, case_id: str, graph: Graph, expected: set[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
+    python = python_oracle(graph)
+    shacl = shape_oracle(graph)
+    if python != shacl or python != expected:
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"{kind}/{case_id}: expected={sorted(expected)}, "
+            f"python={sorted(python)}, shacl={sorted(shacl)}"
+        )
+    return {
+        "expected": sorted(expected),
+        "id": case_id,
+        "kind": kind,
+        "python": sorted(python),
+        "shacl": sorted(shacl),
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output",
+        type=Path,
+        default=ROOT / "research/move2/measurements.json",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    started = time.perf_counter()
+    results = [
+        _run_case("corpus", case_id, _fixture_graph(case_id), expected)
+        for case_id, expected in CORPUS_EXPECTED.items()
+    ]
+    results.extend(
+        _run_case("mutation", case_id, graph, expected)
+        for case_id, (graph, expected) in mutation_cases().items()
+    )
+    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
+    peak = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
+    peak_mib = peak / (1024 * 1024) if sys.platform == "darwin" else peak / 1024
+    summary = {
+        "corpusCases": sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
+        "corpusRuleChecks": 4 * sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
+        "elapsedSeconds": round(elapsed, 3),
+        "engine": "pySHACL 0.31.0",
+        "mutationCases": sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
+        "mutationRuleChecks": 4
+        * sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
+        "peakRssMiB": round(peak_mib, 1),
+        "results": results,
+        "status": "PASS",
+    }
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+    print(
+        f"move-2 oracle PASS: {summary['corpusCases']} corpus + "
+        f"{summary['mutationCases']} mutation cases in {summary['elapsedSeconds']}s; "
+        f"peak RSS {summary['peakRssMiB']} MiB"
+    )
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+def test_copy_and_run_validator_imports_no_rulespec_or_refspec_package() -> None:
+    source = (BINDING / "tools" / "validate.py").read_text()
+    tree = ast.parse(source)
+    imported: set[str] = set()
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
+            imported.update(alias.name.split(".", 1)[0] for alias in node.names)
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and node.module:
+            imported.add(node.module.split(".", 1)[0])
+    assert "refspec" not in imported
+    assert "rulespec_conformance" not in imported

codex
I found one packaging hazard during the final overlap audit: one generated shape reused the IRI of RuleSpec’s existing hand-authored “complete support” shape, even though the two queries are not identical. They are separated today, but any future consumer loading both graphs would merge the constraints under one node. I’m correcting the generated rule to a distinct, precise IRI before delivery and will rerun the wheel and consumer proofs; this is exactly the sort of drift risk the move is meant to remove.

 # recognizes the nested struct by that member rather than by a marker name.

+SHACL_SPARQL_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(
+    r'(?ms)^#(?P<shape>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*Shape)Sparql:\s*"""\n'
+    r'(?P<body>.*?)\n"""\s*$'
+)
+COMPACT_OR_ABSOLUTE_IRI_RE = re.compile(
+    r"^(?:[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:[^\s]+|<[^\s<>]+>)$"
+)
+
+
+def parse_shacl_sparql_annotations(source: str) -> list[SparqlConstraintDef]:
+    """Parse the fail-closed CUE annotation format for graph rules.
+
+    The definition name supplies the stable shape local name. Its multiline
+    string has a generated-scaffolding header, a literal ``---`` separator,
+    then the SPARQL SELECT query::
+
+        #ExampleShapeSparql: <CUE multiline string>
+          targetClass: rkaf:Example
+          message: Explanation shown in a SHACL result.
+          ---
+          PREFIX rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#>
+          SELECT $this WHERE { ... }
+
+    Repeating ``targetClass`` is allowed. Everything else is rejected rather
+    than silently omitted from the emitted constraint.
+    """
+
+    constraints: list[SparqlConstraintDef] = []
+    seen: set[str] = set()
+    for match in SHACL_SPARQL_BLOCK_RE.finditer(source):
+        shape_name = match.group("shape")
+        if shape_name in seen:
+            raise CompileError(f"duplicate SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name}")
+        seen.add(shape_name)
+        header, separator, select = match.group("body").partition("\n---\n")
+        if not separator:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no --- query separator"
+            )
+        targets: list[str] = []
+        message: Optional[str] = None
+        for raw_line in header.splitlines():
+            line = raw_line.strip()
+            if not line:
+                continue
+            key, colon, value = line.partition(":")
+            if not colon or not value.strip():
+                raise CompileError(
+                    f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has malformed header {line!r}"
+                )
+            value = value.strip()
+            if key == "targetClass":
+                if not COMPACT_OR_ABSOLUTE_IRI_RE.fullmatch(value):
+                    raise CompileError(
+                        f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has invalid targetClass {value!r}"
+                    )
+                targets.append(value)
+            elif key == "message":
+                if message is not None:
+                    raise CompileError(
+                        f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} repeats message"
+                    )
+                message = value
+            else:
+                raise CompileError(
+                    f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has unknown header {key!r}"
+                )
+        query = select.strip()
+        if not targets:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no targetClass"
+            )
+        if not message:
+            raise CompileError(f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} has no message")
+        if not re.search(r"(?i)\bSELECT\s+(?:DISTINCT\s+)?\$this\b", query):
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} must SELECT $this"
+            )
+        if '"""' in query:
+            raise CompileError(
+                f"SHACL-SPARQL shape {shape_name} contains a Turtle long-string terminator"
+            )
+        constraints.append(
+            SparqlConstraintDef(
+                shape_name=shape_name,
+                target_classes=targets,
+                message=message,
+                select=query,
+            )
+        )
+    return constraints
+

+# ---- SHACL-SPARQL target (annotated relational rules) --------------------
+
+def target_shacl_sparql(doc: ConstraintDoc) -> str:
+    """Emit only the relational rules explicitly carried by this CUE file."""
+
+    out: list[str] = [
+        "# AUTO-GENERATED by tools/constraints_compile.py "
+        "(target=shacl-sparql).",
+        "# Source: " + (
+            _source_relpath(doc.source_file) or str(doc.source_file or "unknown")
+        ),
+        "# DO NOT EDIT: change the #*ShapeSparql annotation in the CUE source.",
+        "",
+        "@prefix sh:   <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .",
+        "@prefix rkaf: <https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#> .",
+        "",
+    ]
+    for constraint in doc.sparql_constraints:
+        out.append(f"rkaf:{constraint.shape_name} a sh:NodeShape ;")
+        for target_class in constraint.target_classes:
+            out.append(f"  sh:targetClass {target_class} ;")
+        out.extend(
+            (
+                "  sh:sparql [",
+                "    a sh:SPARQLConstraint ;",
+                f"    sh:message {json.dumps(constraint.message)} ;",
+                '    sh:select """',
+                constraint.select,
+                '    """ ;',
+                "  ] .",
+                "",
+            )
+        )
+    return "\n".join(out)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Refresh the RuleSpec-owned adjudication shapes vendored into this binding.
+
+The binding validator deliberately imports no RefSpec or RuleSpec package
+code. This development-time generator is the only package-aware side of that
+boundary: it reads compiler output through the installed
+``rulespec_conformance.contract.resources`` accessor, writes plain Turtle
+beside the Atlas shapes, and records exact source and output digests.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from rulespec_conformance.contract import VERSION, resources
+
+BINDING_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+OUTPUT_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"
+LOCK_PATH = BINDING_ROOT / "shapes" / "rulespec-adjudication.lock.json"
+RESOURCE_NAMES = ("machine-adjudication", "resolver-proof-record")
+
+
+def _digest(payload: bytes) -> str:
+    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _canonical_json(value: object) -> bytes:
+    return (
+        json.dumps(
+            value,
+            ensure_ascii=False,
+            allow_nan=False,
+            sort_keys=True,
+            separators=(",", ":"),
+        ).encode("utf-8")
+        + b"\n"
+    )
+
+
+def render() -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
+    parts = [
+        "# GENERATED by tools/refresh_rulespec_adjudication_shapes.py.",
+        "# Source: rulespec-conformance compiler output; do not edit here.",
+        f"# Rulespec contract version: {VERSION}",
+        "",
+    ]
+    source_rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
+    for name in RESOURCE_NAMES:
+        text = resources.shacl_sparql(name, family="analysis")
+        payload = text.encode("utf-8")
+        source_rows.append(
+            {
+                "accessor": (
+                    "rulespec_conformance.contract.resources."
+                    f"shacl_sparql({name!r}, family='analysis')"
+                ),
+                "byteLength": len(payload),
+                "digest": _digest(payload),
+                "name": name,
+            }
+        )
+        parts.extend((text.rstrip(), ""))
+    output = "\n".join(parts).encode("utf-8")
+    lock = _canonical_json(
+        {
+            "format": "RulespecAdjudicationShapeLock",
+            "formatVersion": "1.0",
+            "output": {
+                "byteLength": len(output),
+                "digest": _digest(output),
+                "path": "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl",
+            },
+            "package": "rulespec-conformance",
+            "packageVersion": VERSION,
+            "resources": source_rows,
+        }
+    )
+    return output, lock
+
+
+def _check(path: Path, expected: bytes) -> bool:
+    if not path.is_file():
+        print(f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} is missing")
+        return False
+    observed = path.read_bytes()
+    if observed != expected:
+        print(
+            f"STALE: {path.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} differs "
+            f"(expected {_digest(expected)}, found {_digest(observed)})"
+        )
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--check",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="refuse stale generated data instead of refreshing it",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    output, lock = render()
+    if args.check:
+        return 0 if _check(OUTPUT_PATH, output) and _check(LOCK_PATH, lock) else 1
+    OUTPUT_PATH.write_bytes(output)
+    LOCK_PATH.write_bytes(lock)
+    print(
+        "refreshed "
+        f"{OUTPUT_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)} ({_digest(output)}) and "
+        f"{LOCK_PATH.relative_to(BINDING_ROOT)}"
+    )
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Differential oracle for compiler-emitted adjudication SHACL-SPARQL.
+
+The Python implementation below is copied and reduced from the four relevant
+parts of ``bindings/atlas/3.1/tools/validate.py``. It deliberately imports
+neither that module nor RuleSpec compiler code: importing the implementation
+being replaced would make agreement circular.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import resource
+import sys
+import time
+from itertools import combinations
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from pyshacl import validate as shacl_validate
+from rdflib import Dataset, Graph, Literal, Namespace, URIRef
+from rdflib.namespace import RDF, SH, SKOS
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+BINDING = ROOT / "bindings/atlas/3.1"
+FIXTURES = BINDING / "fixtures"
+SHAPES_PATH = BINDING / "shapes/rulespec-adjudication.shacl.ttl"
+
+RKAF = Namespace("https://rulespec.org/ns/v1#")
+CASE = Namespace("urn:ref:move2-oracle:")
+
+RULE_SHAPES = {
+    "independence": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationFiveAxisIndependenceShape,
+    "complete-support": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationCompleteSupportShape,
+    "verdict-lattice": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationVerdictLatticeFoldShape,
+    "proof-replay": RKAF.MachineAdjudicationProofReplayShape,
+}
+
+CORPUS_EXPECTED = {
+    "adjudication-single-proof": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-validator-actor": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-independence-group": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-provider": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-provider-model": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-same-response-artifact": {"independence"},
+    "adjudication-discarded-support": {"complete-support"},
+    "adjudication-relation-not-licensed": {"verdict-lattice"},
+    "adjudication-verdicts-disagree": {"verdict-lattice"},
+    "adjudication-foreign-comparison": {"proof-replay"},
+    "all-resource-profiles": set(),
+    "qualified-three-machine-support": set(),
+    "qualified-lattice-branches": set(),
+    "adjudication-refused-comparison-record": set(),
+}
+
+
+def _one(graph: Graph, subject: URIRef, predicate: URIRef) -> object:
+    values = list(graph.objects(subject, predicate))
+    if len(values) != 1:
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"oracle input requires one {predicate} on {subject}; found {len(values)}"
+        )
+    return values[0]
+
+
+def _fold_verdicts(verdicts: frozenset[object]) -> URIRef | None:
+    """Copied oracle for validate.py::_adjudicated_relation."""
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictSame}:
+        return SKOS.exactMatch
+    if verdicts <= {RKAF.verdictSame, RKAF.verdictNearSame} and (
+        RKAF.verdictNearSame in verdicts
+    ):
+        return SKOS.closeMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetBroader}:
+        return SKOS.broadMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower}:
+        return SKOS.narrowMatch
+    if verdicts == {RKAF.verdictRelated}:
+        return SKOS.relatedMatch
+    return None
+
+
+def python_oracle(graph: Graph) -> set[str]:
+    """Verdicts from the copied old Python behavior for the four rules."""
+    violations: set[str] = set()
+    comparisons = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    proofs = set(graph.subjects(RDF.type, RKAF.ResolverProofRecord))
+
+    for proof in proofs:
+        comparison = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofComparisonContext)
+        if proof not in set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord)):
+            violations.add("complete-support")
+        citing = {
+            subject
+            for subject in graph.subjects(RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, proof)
+            if subject in comparisons
+        }
+        if len(citing) > 1:
+            violations.add("proof-replay")
+
+    for comparison in comparisons:
+        if _one(graph, comparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome) != RKAF.comparisonSatisfied:
+            continue
+        cited = set(graph.objects(comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord))
+        facts: list[tuple[object, ...]] = []
+        for proof in cited:
+            issuer = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.proofIssuer)
+            lineage = _one(graph, proof, RKAF.hasAILineage)
+            facts.append(
+                (
+                    issuer,
+                    _one(graph, proof, RKAF.independenceGroup),
+                    _one(graph, issuer, RKAF.proofResolver),
+                    str(_one(graph, lineage, RKAF.modelId)),
+                    _one(graph, proof, RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact),
+                )
+            )
+        if not any(
+            all(left[index] != right[index] for index in range(5))
+            for left, right in combinations(facts, 2)
+        ):
+            violations.add("independence")
+
+        assertion = _one(graph, comparison, RKAF.comparisonExpectedAssertion)
+        stated_relation = _one(graph, assertion, RDF.predicate)
+        verdicts = frozenset(
+            _one(graph, proof, RKAF.adjudicationVerdict) for proof in cited
+        )
+        if _fold_verdicts(verdicts) != stated_relation:
+            violations.add("verdict-lattice")
+    return violations
+
+
+def shape_oracle(graph: Graph) -> set[str]:
+    """Run each emitted rule alone so its Boolean verdict has a stable ID."""
+    all_shapes = Graph().parse(SHAPES_PATH, format="turtle")
+    target_predicates = (
+        SH.targetClass,
+        SH.targetNode,
+        SH.targetSubjectsOf,
+        SH.targetObjectsOf,
+    )
+    violations: set[str] = set()
+    for rule, keep in RULE_SHAPES.items():
+        shapes = Graph()
+        for triple in all_shapes:
+            shapes.add(triple)
+        for predicate in target_predicates:
+            for subject, obj in list(shapes.subject_objects(predicate)):
+                if subject != keep:
+                    shapes.remove((subject, predicate, obj))
+        conforms, _, _ = shacl_validate(
+            graph,
+            shacl_graph=shapes,
+            inference="none",
+            advanced=True,
+            inplace=False,
+            abort_on_first=False,
+            meta_shacl=False,
+        )
+        if not conforms:
+            violations.add(rule)
+    return violations
+
+
+def _fixture_path(case_id: str) -> Path:
+    corpus = json.loads((FIXTURES / "corpus.json").read_bytes())
+    row = next(row for row in corpus["cases"] if row["id"] == case_id)
+    return FIXTURES / row["path"]
+
+
+def _fixture_graph(case_id: str) -> Graph:
+    root = _fixture_path(case_id)
+    if not root.is_dir():
+        raise SystemExit(
+            f"fixture {case_id} is not built; run "
+            "bindings/atlas/3.1/tools/build_fixtures.py first"
+        )
+    manifest = json.loads((root / "atlas-manifest.json").read_bytes())
+    asserted_id = URIRef(
+        next(row["id"] for row in manifest["graphs"] if row["role"] == "asserted")
+    )
+    dataset = Dataset()
+    for pack in manifest["packs"]:
+        payload = (root / pack["path"]).read_bytes()
+        if pack["transport"]["compression"] == "zstd":
+            try:
+                from compression import zstd
+            except ImportError:
+                from backports import zstd
+            payload = zstd.decompress(payload)
+        dataset.parse(data=payload.decode("utf-8"), format="nquads")
+    source = dataset.graph(asserted_id)
+    graph = Graph()
+    for triple in source:
+        graph.add(triple)
+    return graph
+
+
+def _add_proof(graph: Graph, key: str, *, cite: bool = True) -> URIRef:
+    proof = CASE[f"proof-{key}"]
+    issuer = CASE[f"issuer-{key}"]
+    lineage = CASE[f"lineage-{key}"]
+    graph.add((proof, RDF.type, RKAF.ResolverProofRecord))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.proofComparisonContext, CASE.comparison))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.proofIssuer, issuer))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.independenceGroup, CASE[f"group-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.hasAILineage, lineage))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact, CASE[f"response-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((proof, RKAF.adjudicationVerdict, RKAF.verdictSame))
+    graph.add((issuer, RKAF.proofResolver, CASE[f"provider-{key}"]))
+    graph.add((lineage, RKAF.modelId, Literal(f"model-{key}")))
+    if cite:
+        graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, proof))
+    return proof
+
+
+def _base_graph() -> Graph:
+    graph = Graph()
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome, RKAF.comparisonSatisfied))
+    graph.add((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonExpectedAssertion, CASE.assertion))
+    graph.add((CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.exactMatch))
+    _add_proof(graph, "alpha")
+    _add_proof(graph, "beta")
+    return graph
+
+
+def _clone(graph: Graph) -> Graph:
+    result = Graph()
+    for triple in graph:
+        result.add(triple)
+    return result
+
+
+def _replace(graph: Graph, subject: URIRef, predicate: URIRef, value: object) -> None:
+    graph.remove((subject, predicate, None))
+    graph.add((subject, predicate, value))
+
+
+def mutation_cases() -> dict[str, tuple[Graph, set[str]]]:
+    base = _base_graph()
+    cases: dict[str, tuple[Graph, set[str]]] = {"valid-exact": (base, set())}
+
+    single = _clone(base)
+    single.remove((CASE["proof-beta"], None, None))
+    single.remove((CASE.comparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, CASE["proof-beta"]))
+    cases["single-proof"] = (single, {"independence"})
+
+    axis_changes = {
+        "same-actor": (CASE["proof-beta"], RKAF.proofIssuer, CASE["issuer-alpha"]),
+        "same-group": (
+            CASE["proof-beta"],
+            RKAF.independenceGroup,
+            CASE["group-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-response": (
+            CASE["proof-beta"],
+            RKAF.sealedResponseArtifact,
+            CASE["response-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-provider": (
+            CASE["issuer-beta"],
+            RKAF.proofResolver,
+            CASE["provider-alpha"],
+        ),
+        "same-model": (
+            CASE["lineage-beta"],
+            RKAF.modelId,
+            Literal("model-alpha"),
+        ),
+    }
+    for name, (subject, predicate, value) in axis_changes.items():
+        graph = _clone(base)
+        _replace(graph, subject, predicate, value)
+        cases[name] = (graph, {"independence"})
+
+    discarded = _clone(base)
+    _add_proof(discarded, "gamma", cite=False)
+    cases["discarded-support"] = (discarded, {"complete-support"})
+
+    replay = _clone(base)
+    replay.add((CASE.otherComparison, RDF.type, RKAF.RelationComparisonContext))
+    replay.add((CASE.otherComparison, RKAF.comparisonOutcome, RKAF.comparisonRefused))
+    replay.add(
+        (CASE.otherComparison, RKAF.comparisonProofRecord, CASE["proof-alpha"])
+    )
+    cases["proof-replay"] = (replay, {"proof-replay"})
+
+    mixed_exact = _clone(base)
+    _replace(
+        mixed_exact,
+        CASE["proof-beta"],
+        RKAF.adjudicationVerdict,
+        RKAF.verdictNearSame,
+    )
+    cases["exact-with-near"] = (mixed_exact, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    valid_close = _clone(mixed_exact)
+    _replace(valid_close, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.closeMatch)
+    cases["valid-close"] = (valid_close, set())
+
+    close_without_near = _clone(base)
+    _replace(close_without_near, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, SKOS.closeMatch)
+    cases["close-without-near"] = (close_without_near, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    branches = (
+        ("valid-broad", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetBroader, set()),
+        ("valid-narrow", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictTargetNarrower, set()),
+        ("valid-related", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictRelated, set()),
+        ("broad-with-same", SKOS.broadMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+        ("narrow-with-same", SKOS.narrowMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+        ("related-with-same", SKOS.relatedMatch, RKAF.verdictSame, {"verdict-lattice"}),
+    )
+    for name, relation, verdict, expected in branches:
+        graph = _clone(base)
+        _replace(graph, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, relation)
+        for key in ("alpha", "beta"):
+            _replace(
+                graph,
+                CASE[f"proof-{key}"],
+                RKAF.adjudicationVerdict,
+                verdict,
+            )
+        cases[name] = (graph, expected)
+
+    unknown = _clone(base)
+    _replace(unknown, CASE.assertion, RDF.predicate, CASE.unsupportedRelation)
+    cases["unsupported-relation"] = (unknown, {"verdict-lattice"})
+
+    refused = _clone(mixed_exact)
+    _replace(
+        refused,
+        CASE.comparison,
+        RKAF.comparisonOutcome,
+        RKAF.comparisonRefused,
+    )
+    cases["refused-does-not-fold"] = (refused, set())
+    return cases
+
+
+def _run_case(kind: str, case_id: str, graph: Graph, expected: set[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
+    python = python_oracle(graph)
+    shacl = shape_oracle(graph)
+    if python != shacl or python != expected:
+        raise AssertionError(
+            f"{kind}/{case_id}: expected={sorted(expected)}, "
+            f"python={sorted(python)}, shacl={sorted(shacl)}"
+        )
+    return {
+        "expected": sorted(expected),
+        "id": case_id,
+        "kind": kind,
+        "python": sorted(python),
+        "shacl": sorted(shacl),
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output",
+        type=Path,
+        default=ROOT / "research/move2/measurements.json",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    started = time.perf_counter()
+    results = [
+        _run_case("corpus", case_id, _fixture_graph(case_id), expected)
+        for case_id, expected in CORPUS_EXPECTED.items()
+    ]
+    results.extend(
+        _run_case("mutation", case_id, graph, expected)
+        for case_id, (graph, expected) in mutation_cases().items()
+    )
+    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
+    peak = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
+    peak_mib = peak / (1024 * 1024) if sys.platform == "darwin" else peak / 1024
+    summary = {
+        "corpusCases": sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
+        "corpusRuleChecks": 4 * sum(row["kind"] == "corpus" for row in results),
+        "elapsedSeconds": round(elapsed, 3),
+        "engine": "pySHACL 0.31.0",
+        "mutationCases": sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
+        "mutationRuleChecks": 4
+        * sum(row["kind"] == "mutation" for row in results),
+        "peakRssMiB": round(peak_mib, 1),
+        "results": results,
+        "status": "PASS",
+    }
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+    print(
+        f"move-2 oracle PASS: {summary['corpusCases']} corpus + "
+        f"{summary['mutationCases']} mutation cases in {summary['elapsedSeconds']}s; "
+        f"peak RSS {summary['peakRssMiB']} MiB"
+    )
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
